The notes also add coverage for: "Phase 1 bootstrap guidance covers both aimgr-present/package-missing and aimgr-missing/manual-install branches," "Phase 1 asks for or preserves the intended project mode early enough for the handoff to work," and "all important plugin flows still work under the split."

**Why**: This was the most critical acceptance gap. It is now covered.

**Suggested action**: None. The acceptance review notes are comprehensive.

title: Implement minimal bootstrap-only runtime init flow
description:
## Description
Refactor the runtime `/opencode-coder/init` behavior so plugin code contains only a minimal bootstrap flow for the pre-resource phase. The bootstrap prompt may guide prerequisite checks and installation, but it must not contain the full durable init/setup workflow that belongs in markdown commands, skills, and references.

## Instructions
1. Replace the current long runtime init template with a minimal bootstrap-only flow.
2. Keep the runtime init flow limited to concerns that truly require pre-resource code support, such as:
   - detecting missing prerequisites
   - guiding installation of git, beads CLI, aimgr, and the opencode-coder package when needed
   - helping the user reach a Phase 2-capable state
3. Ensure the bootstrap flow can continue in the same session when resources become available, handing off to the normal markdown/skill workflow rather than duplicating it in code.
4. Preserve the behavior that the plugin remains usable even if the user chooses not to install the resources, while making the degraded state clear.
5. Remove any normal-operation setup, docs-lifecycle, AGENTS-generation, or mode-transition procedure text from the runtime bootstrap template.

## Files to Modify
- src/templates/init-install-guide.ts — replace the long init workflow with a minimal bootstrap template, or replace/remove this file if a better bootstrap-only structure is clearer
- src/templates/index.ts — update exports if the bootstrap template structure changes
- src/index.ts — keep runtime init registration aligned with the bootstrap-only model

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Runtime `/opencode-coder/init` content is minimal and bootstrap-only
- [ ] Runtime init no longer embeds the durable normal-operation workflow
- [ ] The bootstrap path can hand off to Phase 2 in the same session when resources become available
- [ ] The plugin still behaves sensibly when the user does not complete installation
close_reason: Implemented and verified as part of phase split work

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Bootstrap template must still ask for mode — but the task does not acknowledge this

**What**: The current init template (343 lines) asks the user to choose stealth/team/inactive mode in Step 2 before doing any beads initialization. The md6.2 task says "Replace the current long runtime init template with a minimal bootstrap-only flow" and limits it to "detecting missing prerequisites, guiding installation... helping the user reach a Phase 2-capable state." Mode selection is not mentioned as a bootstrap concern.

**Why**: Mode selection MUST happen before resources are installed in many flows. The aimgr autoInitialize flow only runs in active modes. If a user runs `/opencode-coder/init` on a fresh project in Phase 1, the bootstrap flow must ask what mode they want before it can meaningfully install anything or write `.coder/opencode-coder.yaml`. If mode selection is stripped from the bootstrap template, the flow is broken for fresh projects: the plugin can't activate, so aimgr won't auto-install, so resources won't appear, so Phase 2 won't be reached.

**Suggested action**: Explicitly state that mode selection (stealth/team/inactive/disabled) is a bootstrap concern that must remain in the Phase 1 init flow. The instructions should list it as one of the "concerns that truly require pre-resource code support" alongside prerequisite detection and installation guidance.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## "Hand off to Phase 2 in the same session" is mechanically unclear

**What**: Acceptance criterion says "The bootstrap path can hand off to Phase 2 in the same session when resources become available." Instruction 3 says "Ensure the bootstrap flow can continue in the same session when resources become available, handing off to the normal markdown/skill workflow rather than duplicating it in code."

**Why**: This is the hardest part of the entire epic and it has zero implementation guidance. Consider the concrete scenario: user runs `/opencode-coder/init` on a fresh project in Phase 1. The bootstrap asks to install aimgr resources. User says yes. `aimgr install package/opencode-coder` runs. Now markdown command files exist on disk — but the OpenCode session's command registry was populated at startup. The resource-backed `/opencode-coder/init` command (from `init.md`) is not registered because it was not present at plugin load time. The `opencode-coder` skill is now on disk but was not in the skill catalog when the session started.

So what does "hand off" mean? Does it mean:
- (A) The bootstrap template tells the agent to load the skill using `skill()` tool call? This might work for skills but won't register new commands.
- (B) The bootstrap template includes enough inline text to replicate what the skill would do? This violates the "no workflow duplication" goal.
- (C) The bootstrap says "restart OpenCode to complete setup"? This violates the same-session handoff requirement.

**Suggested action**: The task must specify the handoff mechanism. The most practical option is (A): the bootstrap template instructs the agent to load the `opencode-coder` skill via tool call after resources are installed. The skill then provides the workflow. New commands will only be available after restart, which is acceptable and should be stated explicitly. But this must be written in the task, not left to discovery during implementation.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## "Behaves sensibly when the user does not complete installation" is vague

**What**: Acceptance criterion says "The plugin still behaves sensibly when the user does not complete installation." Instruction 4 says "Preserve the behavior that the plugin remains usable even if the user chooses not to install the resources, while making the degraded state clear."

**Why**: "Behaves sensibly" and "remains usable" are not testable. The current init template handles this with specific text ("if they decline, provide the commands for them to run manually"). What should the bootstrap do in Phase 1 if the user declines everything? Currently, the plugin just shows `/opencode-coder/init` and nothing else for inactive projects. Should that remain the behavior? Should there be a toast? A log message? The acceptance criteria need to be testable.

**Suggested action**: Replace "behaves sensibly" with concrete expectations:
- The plugin returns only `/opencode-coder/init` when in Phase 1
- No error toasts are shown for users who choose to stay in Phase 1
- The user can re-run `/opencode-coder/init` at any time to try again
- Active-mode commands (`/docs`, `/improve-doc`) remain suppressed until Phase 2 is reached

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Beads initialization, git init, and bd CLI guidance must stay in bootstrap — but are not listed

**What**: The task limits bootstrap to "detecting missing prerequisites, guiding installation of git, beads CLI, aimgr, and the opencode-coder package." This is good — it acknowledges git and beads CLI. But it also says "Remove any normal-operation setup, docs-lifecycle, AGENTS-generation, or mode-transition procedure text from the runtime bootstrap template." The current template contains beads initialization (Step 3: `bd init --stealth && bd hooks install`), stealth exclusion setup, and mode transitions (stealth→team, team→stealth). These are not docs-lifecycle or AGENTS-generation, but they ARE multi-step procedures.

**Why**: If beads initialization is Phase 2 work (handled by the skill), then the bootstrap can be truly minimal. But if beads init must happen before resources are installed (e.g., for the `ecosystemReady` flag to become true), then it is a Phase 1 concern and must stay in the bootstrap. The task doesn't say which.

**Suggested action**: Explicitly classify each current init template step as Phase 1 or Phase 2:
- Step 1 (detect startup state): Phase 1 bootstrap ✓
- Step 2 (choose mode): Phase 1 bootstrap (see other comment)
- Step 3 (beads init): Phase 1 or Phase 2? → decide and state
- Step 4 (AGENTS.md): Phase 2 (skill-backed) ✓
- Step 5 (docs lifecycle): Phase 2 (skill-backed) ✓
- Step 6 (report): Phase 2 ✓
- Mode transitions (stealth↔team): Phase 1 or Phase 2? → decide and state

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Re-review: Mode selection in Phase 1 bootstrap — RESOLVED

**What**: The previous review's critical finding was that mode selection (stealth/team/inactive/disabled) was not listed as a Phase 1 bootstrap concern. The notes now explicitly state: "Ask for the desired project mode during Phase 1 bootstrapping so the install path knows the target state. Cover fresh projects and already-disabled/inactive projects appropriately."

The epic-level notes also say: "Phase 1 must gather or confirm the desired project mode early enough for the install-to-Phase-2 handoff to work correctly, including stealth, team, and remaining inactive/disabled where appropriate."

**Why**: This was the most important missing piece for the bootstrap flow. It is now captured.

**Suggested action**: None. Previous critical concern is addressed.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Re-review: Same-session handoff mechanism — RESOLVED by restart-based design

**What**: The previous review flagged that "hand off to Phase 2 in the same session" had zero implementation guidance and was mechanically impossible (new commands can't be registered mid-session). The epic notes now resolve this cleanly: "If Phase 1 installs the missing resources successfully, the bootstrap flow should tell the user to restart or reopen OpenCode and then run `/opencode-coder/init` again so the Phase 2 workflow can take over cleanly."

The md6.2 notes confirm: "After Phase 1 successfully installs the needed resources, do not duplicate Phase 2 logic in code. Instead, instruct the user to restart or reopen OpenCode and rerun `/opencode-coder/init` so the markdown/skill-backed Phase 2 workflow handles the rest."

**Why**: This eliminates the impossible same-session handoff requirement. The bootstrap installs resources, then tells the user to restart. On next session, the plugin sees resources on disk, classifies as Phase 2, and the resource-backed init.md takes over. This is mechanically sound.

**Suggested action**: The acceptance criterion "The bootstrap path can hand off to Phase 2 in the same session when resources become available" in the md6.2 description should be updated to match the restart-based design in the notes. Currently the description says same-session, the notes say restart. This is a contradiction — but the notes take precedence. The implementer should follow the notes. This is a minor cleanup.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Re-review: "Behaves sensibly" acceptance criterion still vague — downgraded to MINOR

**What**: The md6.2 acceptance criterion still says "The plugin still behaves sensibly when the user does not complete installation." The notes add: "The plugin must remain usable in a degraded state when the user declines installation, but the degraded state should be explicit." This is better but still not concrete.

**Why**: An implementer can now understand the intent (explicit degraded state, not broken), but "explicit" leaves room for interpretation. Does explicit mean a log message? A toast? A different init template that says "You are in degraded mode"? The previous review suggested specific expectations (only init registered, no error toasts, re-runnable). The notes partially address this with "keep the bootstrap content minimal" but don't specify the degraded-state UX.

**Suggested action**: This is now a minor gap. The intent is clear enough. The implementer will likely do the obvious thing: show only `/opencode-coder/init` and suppress active commands. If you want to nail this down further, add: "When the user declines installation, the plugin exposes only `/opencode-coder/init` with no error toasts or warnings." But this is no longer blocking.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Re-review: Beads init / mode transitions — Phase 1 vs Phase 2 classification still missing

**What**: The previous review asked for an explicit classification of each current init template step as Phase 1 or Phase 2. The notes added to md6.2 say "Keep the bootstrap content minimal: no embedded normal-operation docs lifecycle, AGENTS generation, or long mode-transition procedures." This tells us what is NOT in Phase 1, but it does not say where beads initialization (`bd init --stealth && bd hooks install`) and mode transitions (stealth↔team) live.

The current init template has 343 lines covering beads init (Step 3), AGENTS.md creation (Step 4), docs lifecycle (Step 5), mode transitions, and completion reporting (Step 6). The notes say Steps 4-6 are Phase 2 (skill-backed). But Step 3 (beads init) and the mode transition workflows are not classified.

**Why**: Beads initialization and mode transitions are multi-step procedures involving shell commands, file moves, and git operations. They are not "docs lifecycle" or "AGENTS generation" so they don't fall under the explicit exclusion. But they are also not "prerequisite detection" or "installation guidance." The implementer must decide: does the Phase 1 bootstrap template include `bd init --stealth && bd hooks install` and the stealth↔team transition workflows, or are those Phase 2 skill-backed concerns?

If beads init is Phase 2 (skill-backed), then the Phase 1 bootstrap can be truly minimal: detect state → ask mode → install aimgr resources → tell user to restart. This is the cleanest split.

If beads init is Phase 1 (must happen before resources install), then the bootstrap template grows significantly and includes multi-step shell procedures — undermining the "minimal bootstrap" goal.

**Suggested action**: Add an explicit decision to the notes. My recommendation: beads init and mode transitions belong in Phase 2 (the skill handles them after resources are available). Phase 1 only needs to: detect state, ask mode, write `.coder/opencode-coder.yaml`, install aimgr resources if requested, and tell the user to restart. This keeps Phase 1 genuinely minimal. But this is a design decision that must be stated, not left to implementer judgment.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Re-review: Description vs notes contradiction on same-session handoff

**What**: md6.2 description instruction 3 says: "Ensure the bootstrap flow can continue in the same session when resources become available, handing off to the normal markdown/skill workflow rather than duplicating it in code." Acceptance criterion 3 says: "The bootstrap path can hand off to Phase 2 in the same session when resources become available."

The notes say: "After Phase 1 successfully installs the needed resources, do not duplicate Phase 2 logic in code. Instead, instruct the user to restart or reopen OpenCode and rerun `/opencode-coder/init`."

These directly contradict each other. The description says same-session handoff; the notes say restart.

**Why**: The implementer will see both. One says "continue in this session" and the other says "restart." The notes are more recent and represent the reviewed/decided design, but the description has not been updated to match. This will cause confusion.

**Suggested action**: The description's instruction 3 and acceptance criterion 3 should be updated to match the restart-based handoff design. Replace "continue in the same session" with "instruct the user to restart OpenCode and rerun `/opencode-coder/init`." This is a description cleanup, not a design change.

title: Remove hardcoded normal-operation command prompts from plugin code
description:
## Description
Remove hardcoded normal-operation prompt text for the opencode-coder command set from `src/` so Phase 2 behavior is sourced from markdown commands, skills, and references instead of TypeScript string templates.

## Instructions
1. Remove the inline runtime workflow templates for `/opencode-coder/docs` and `/opencode-coder/improve-doc` from `src/index.ts`.
2. Remove any remaining hardcoded normal-operation workflow text in `src/` that duplicates command/skill/reference behavior.
3. Keep only operational runtime logic in code, such as command registration, suppression, gating, resource checks, and bootstrap fallback.
4. Ensure that once the plugin is in Phase 2, the command surfaces come from the markdown/resource model instead of embedded code strings.
5. If any runtime-generated text must remain for technical reasons, keep it minimal and operational rather than instructional.

## Files to Modify
- src/index.ts — remove hardcoded normal-operation prompt strings and keep only operational registration logic
- src/templates/**/*.ts — remove or reduce any normal-operation instruction text still embedded in templates
- other files under src/ only if they contain duplicate workflow prompt text

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `src/index.ts` no longer embeds the normal-operation docs/improve-doc workflow prompts
- [ ] `src/` contains no hardcoded normal-operation command workflow text for the opencode-coder command set
- [ ] Runtime code retains only operational logic and any minimal bootstrap fallback needed before resources exist
- [ ] Phase 2 behavior is sourced from markdown/resources rather than TypeScript prompt strings
close_reason: Implemented and verified as part of phase split work

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Scope is clear but the boundary with resource-backed commands is not

**What**: The task says to remove the `DOCS_LIFECYCLE_COMMAND_DEFINITIONS` from `src/index.ts` (the hardcoded `opencode-coder/docs` and `opencode-coder/improve-doc` templates). This is clearly correct — those are workflow prompts that belong in markdown commands. But the task also says "Remove any remaining hardcoded normal-operation workflow text in `src/` that duplicates command/skill/reference behavior."

**Why**: The current code in `src/index.ts` lines 21-60 contains `DOCS_LIFECYCLE_COMMAND_DEFINITIONS` with template strings that will be replaced by the resource-backed markdown commands. But after removal, the gating logic (lines 273-297) that decides whether to register these commands still needs to know the command names. The task should clarify: after removing the hardcoded templates, does the `config` hook still need to conditionally register/suppress these commands? Or does it just let the resource-backed commands through unconditionally?

**Suggested action**: Clarify the post-removal behavior. The most likely correct answer is: the `config` hook should still suppress resource-backed docs lifecycle commands when `resourcesHealthy` is false (or when in Phase 1). But the suppression logic should reference command names, not contain template text. State this explicitly so the implementer knows the runtime gating logic survives even when the templates are removed.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## The init command has a dual existence — the task does not address this conflict

**What**: `/opencode-coder/init` currently exists in TWO places:
1. **Runtime-registered**: via `getInstallGuideTemplate()` in `src/templates/init-install-guide.ts`, always registered by the plugin regardless of phase
2. **Resource-backed**: via `ai-resources/commands/opencode-coder/init.md`, installed by aimgr, which is a 7-line thin wrapper that says "Load the skill, run the init workflow"

The task says "Remove any remaining hardcoded normal-operation workflow text in `src/` that duplicates command/skill/reference behavior." But the runtime-registered `/opencode-coder/init` is NOT duplicating normal-operation behavior — it IS the bootstrap flow. The resource-backed `init.md` is the Phase 2 version.

**Why**: After this epic, in Phase 2 the runtime-registered init command (bootstrap template) will conflict with the resource-backed init command (skill-backed wrapper). Which one wins? Does the runtime registration override the resource-backed one? Do they merge? This collision is not addressed anywhere in the epic.

**Suggested action**: Add explicit instructions for how the init command is handled across phases:
- Phase 1: runtime registers `/opencode-coder/init` with the bootstrap template (as today)
- Phase 2: the resource-backed `/opencode-coder/init` from `init.md` takes over; the runtime should either (a) not register its own version when resources exist, or (b) still register but with content that defers to the skill

This is a critical architectural decision that must not be left to the implementer.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Re-review: Init command dual existence — RESOLVED in notes

**What**: The previous review's critical finding was that no task addressed what happens when both the runtime-registered `/opencode-coder/init` (bootstrap) and the resource-backed `init.md` (Phase 2) exist. The md6.3 notes now state: "Resolve the init lifecycle explicitly in code: runtime `/opencode-coder/init` exists only for Phase 1 bootstrap; once Phase 2 resources are available, normal init behavior must come from the resource-backed markdown command rather than the runtime bootstrap template."

The epic notes confirm: "`/opencode-coder/init` intentionally has two forms: Phase 1: runtime bootstrap init, Phase 2: markdown/resource-backed init."

**Why**: This is now an explicit design decision: the runtime only registers its init in Phase 1, and defers to the resource-backed version in Phase 2. The implementer knows the rule. The gating logic from md6.1's phase classification drives this.

**Suggested action**: None. The previous critical concern is resolved. The implementation is straightforward: in the `config` hook, only register the runtime init command when the phase classification says Phase 1.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Re-review: Post-removal gating logic — still needs one sentence of clarification

**What**: The previous review asked: after removing the hardcoded `DOCS_LIFECYCLE_COMMAND_DEFINITIONS` templates, does the `config` hook still suppress resource-backed docs/improve-doc commands when in Phase 1? The notes say "Keep runtime code limited to registration, suppression, gating, resource checks, and any minimal bootstrap-only generated text." This implicitly says yes — suppression logic survives. But it doesn't explicitly say "the config hook must still delete resource-backed docs/improve-doc commands from the input when in Phase 1."

**Why**: Currently, `src/index.ts` lines 284-289 delete `opencode-coder/docs` and `opencode-coder/improve-doc` from the command registry when `docsLifecycleResourcesAvailable` is false. After md6.3 removes the `DOCS_LIFECYCLE_COMMAND_DEFINITIONS` constant, the deletion logic must remain (it operates on command names, not templates). But the task says "Remove hardcoded normal-operation prompt text" — and an implementer might remove the deletion logic too, thinking it's part of the "hardcoded" behavior.

**Suggested action**: Add one sentence to the notes: "The suppression/deletion of resource-backed docs lifecycle commands by name when in Phase 1 or when resources are unhealthy must be preserved — only the template strings are removed." This is minor but prevents a subtle regression.

title: Update runtime tests for bootstrap and normal-operation phases
description:
## Description
Update the test suite so it validates the new two-phase runtime model instead of the old embedded command-template behavior.

## Instructions
1. Update integration tests that currently assert old hardcoded command template content.
2. Add or adjust tests so they verify both phases:
   - Phase 1 bootstrap behavior before required resources are available
   - Phase 2 normal operation once the expected resources are available
3. Cover the important runtime variants, including:
   - disabled mode
   - stealth mode vs team mode behavior where relevant
   - the standard aimgr/package installation path
   - equivalent manual resource availability if that is part of the detection contract
   - same-session handoff from bootstrap into normal operation where practical to validate
4. Keep the tests aligned with the markdown/skill source-of-truth architecture rather than old string-template snapshots.
5. Run the relevant validation for changed runtime and test files.

## Files to Modify
- tests/integration/plugin.test.ts — update assertions for the two-phase runtime model
- tests/e2e/opencode.test.ts — extend or adjust scenarios if needed for phase coverage
- runtime test helpers only if needed to express the new phase conditions clearly

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Integration tests no longer assert the old embedded workflow prompts
- [ ] Tests cover Phase 1 bootstrap and Phase 2 normal operation behavior
- [ ] Tests preserve disabled-mode and stealth/team expectations where relevant
- [ ] Relevant validation passes after the test updates
close_reason: Implemented and verified as part of phase split work

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Tests reference old assertion patterns but do not specify new Phase 1/Phase 2 scenarios

**What**: The task says "Update integration tests that currently assert old hardcoded command template content" and "Add or adjust tests so they verify both phases." But the test scenarios listed are generic ("disabled mode, stealth mode vs team mode, aimgr path, manual availability, same-session handoff") and do not describe concrete assertions.

**Why**: The current test suite (`tests/integration/plugin.test.ts`) contains very specific assertions, e.g.:
- `expect(cfg.command?.["opencode-coder/docs"]?.template).toContain("references/project-docs-lifecycle.md")`
- `expect(cfg.command?.["opencode-coder/docs"]?.description).toBe("Inspect, bootstrap...")`

These assert the content of the hardcoded templates that md6.3 is removing. After removal, what should the tests assert instead? That the commands are present but their content comes from resources? That the commands are absent when in Phase 1? The task doesn't say.

**Suggested action**: Add concrete test scenario descriptions. For example:
- Phase 1 + fresh project: only `/opencode-coder/init` registered, init template is bootstrap-only (no workflow prose)
- Phase 1 + active project without resources: `/opencode-coder/init` registered with bootstrap template, `/docs` and `/improve-doc` suppressed
- Phase 2 + active + healthy: `/opencode-coder/init` NOT runtime-registered (resource version takes over), `/docs` and `/improve-doc` pass through from resources
- Phase 2 + active + unhealthy: `/docs` and `/improve-doc` suppressed despite resources existing
- Same-session handoff: after aimgr install mid-session, skill is loadable (if testable)

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## "Same-session handoff" is listed as a test scenario but is likely not testable in integration tests

**What**: Instruction 3 says to cover "same-session handoff from bootstrap into normal operation where practical to validate." The qualification "where practical" suggests uncertainty.

**Why**: Same-session handoff requires that: (1) the plugin starts in Phase 1, (2) the agent runs an aimgr install during the session, (3) the skill becomes loadable. In integration tests, aimgr is mocked. The skill loading tool is an OpenCode runtime concept, not a plugin SDK concept. There is no way for a plugin integration test to validate that the agent successfully loads a newly-installed skill. This scenario is fundamentally an e2e test — or it's not testable at all with the current test infrastructure.

**Suggested action**: Either move the same-session handoff scenario explicitly to e2e (opencode.test.ts) with a concrete description of what to test, or remove it from the integration test task and file a separate test-coverage task for it. Don't leave "where practical" as a weasel phrase for the implementer to skip it silently.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Re-review: Test scenarios now specified in notes — substantially improved

**What**: The notes now list concrete test branches: "aimgr available and package/opencode-coder missing," "aimgr missing," "manually available/copied resources without aimgr," "Phase 1 user-guidance branches," "package-install prompting and early mode selection," and "Phase 2 docs/improve-doc behavior no longer depends on hardcoded runtime prompt strings." comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Re-review: Same-session handoff testability — RESOLVED by restart design

**What**: The previous review noted that same-session handoff is not testable in integration tests. The epic design has now changed to a restart-based handoff, which eliminates the need for a same-session handoff test. What needs testing instead is: (1) Phase 1 installs resources and tells user to restart, (2) on next startup, Phase 2 is detected and resource-backed init takes over.

This is testable in integration tests by mocking the phase classification and verifying the config hook behavior under Phase 1 vs Phase 2 inputs.

**Why**: The testability concern is resolved by the design change.

**Suggested action**: None. The restart-based design makes Phase 1 and Phase 2 independently testable without mid-session state changes.

title: Split plugin bootstrap from resource-backed normal operation
description:
## Description
Define and implement a two-phase architecture for opencode-coder runtime behavior. Phase 1 is a minimal bootstrap layer in plugin code that exists only to detect prerequisites, guide installation, and help the user reach a fully operational state when resources are not yet available. Phase 2 is normal operation, where durable command and workflow instructions live in markdown commands, skills, and references rather than in TypeScript string templates.

## Goals
- Keep plugin runtime code responsible only for operational concerns such as detection, gating, registration, and bootstrap fallback
- Define a well-known resource contract for the commands, skills, and agents the plugin expects, while allowing equivalent manual installation outside aimgr
- Make `/opencode-coder/init` the bootstrap entry point when resources are missing, but keep that bootstrap prompt minimal and transitional
- Ensure that once resources are available, normal operation uses markdown commands, skills, and references instead of hardcoded workflow text in `src/`
- Preserve stealth mode, team mode, disabled mode, and same-session handoff from bootstrap into normal operation

## Success Criteria
- [ ] The runtime cleanly distinguishes Phase 1 bootstrap from Phase 2 normal operation
- [ ] Plugin code contains no hardcoded normal-operation workflow prompts for the opencode-coder command set
- [ ] The bootstrap path documents and detects the required resources and accepts either aimgr/package installation or equivalent manual availability
- [ ] `/opencode-coder/init` remains usable before resources are installed and can guide the user into a fully operational Phase 2 state
- [ ] Tests cover the bootstrap/normal-operation split and preserve mode-dependent behavior
close_reason: Phase split implemented and accepted

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Epic-level: no task addresses the runtime init command collision between Phase 1 and Phase 2

**What**: The epic has 4 implementation tasks: define contract (md6.1), bootstrap init flow (md6.2), remove hardcoded prompts (md6.3), update tests (md6.4). None of them address what happens to the runtime-registered `/opencode-coder/init` command when the resource-backed `init.md` also exists in Phase 2.

Currently, `src/index.ts` line 243 always registers `/opencode-coder/init` via `getInstallGuideTemplate()`. In Phase 2, the resource-backed `init.md` (a 7-line thin wrapper) also wants to provide `/opencode-coder/init`. Who wins? Does the runtime override the resource? Does the resource override the runtime? The OpenCode plugin SDK behavior for this collision is not documented in the epic.

**Why**: If the runtime always registers its own init command, it will always override the resource-backed version, meaning Phase 2 init behavior will always use the bootstrap template rather than the skill-backed workflow. This would completely defeat the purpose of having a resource-backed init command. If the runtime only registers init in Phase 1 and defers to the resource in Phase 2, that logic needs to be implemented somewhere — and no task covers it.

**Suggested action**: Add explicit handling to md6.2 or md6.3:
- In Phase 1: runtime registers `/opencode-coder/init` with the bootstrap template (current behavior)
- In Phase 2: runtime does NOT register `/opencode-coder/init` (or registers a minimal version that defers to the resource-backed command)
- The config hook must gate this registration based on the phase classification from md6.1

This is a missing piece of work that no current task covers.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Epic-level: default_agent (orchestrator) logic depends on ecosystemReady which may change meaning

**What**: The current code (src/index.ts lines 313-341) sets `default_agent = "orchestrator"` when `ecosystemReady === true`. The epic's Phase 2 definition likely overlaps with `ecosystemReady`. If the phase classification changes how `ecosystemReady` is computed (e.g., it now also requires the opencode-coder skill to be present), the default_agent behavior changes as a side effect.

**Why**: The orchestrator agent is resource-backed (installed via aimgr). If Phase 2 detection becomes stricter (requiring specific resource file presence), `ecosystemReady` may become false for projects that currently have it true — changing the orchestrator default_agent behavior as an unintended regression.

**Suggested action**: The epic should explicitly state whether the `ecosystemReady` flag changes, and if so, confirm that the `default_agent = "orchestrator"` logic is still correct. Alternatively, decouple the Phase 2 classification from `ecosystemReady` entirely, using a new field, so existing orchestrator behavior is not affected.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Epic-level: stealth mode AGENTS.md injection is not addressed

**What**: The current code (src/index.ts lines 229-238) injects `.coder/AGENTS.md` into `input.instructions` for stealth mode. This is operational runtime logic (not a workflow prompt), so it should survive the refactor. But no task mentions it, and the acceptance criteria don't check for it.

**Why**: If a task implementer aggressively strips things from `src/index.ts`, this injection could be accidentally removed. It is not a "hardcoded workflow prompt" — it is a config hook that injects an instruction file. But the boundary is not stated anywhere, so an implementer following "remove hardcoded normal-operation workflow text" could misinterpret this as workflow text and remove it.

**Suggested action**: Add a note to md6.3 explicitly preserving this as operational runtime logic. Or add an acceptance criterion to md6.5 that verifies stealth AGENTS.md injection still works after the refactor.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Epic-level: can this be simplified from 4 implementation tasks to 2-3?

**What**: The current breakdown is:
1. md6.1: Define resource contract and phase detection
2. md6.2: Implement minimal bootstrap-only init flow
3. md6.3: Remove hardcoded normal-operation command prompts
4. md6.4: Update tests
5. md6.5: Acceptance review

Tasks md6.2 and md6.3 are tightly coupled. md6.3 removes the `DOCS_LIFECYCLE_COMMAND_DEFINITIONS` templates and md6.2 replaces the init template. Both modify `src/index.ts`. Both depend on md6.1. Both are blocked by each other in spirit: you can't safely remove the hardcoded docs commands (md6.3) without knowing whether the bootstrap init still references them (md6.2), and vice versa.

**Why**: Splitting tightly-coupled changes across tasks creates integration risk. The implementer of md6.3 needs to know the exact shape of the bootstrap template from md6.2 to avoid breaking the gating logic. Running them as separate tasks increases the chance of a conflicting intermediate state.

**Suggested action**: Consider merging md6.2 and md6.3 into a single task: "Replace runtime command templates with bootstrap-only init and resource-backed gating." This makes the coupling explicit and ensures both changes are implemented atomically. The test update (md6.4) stays separate because it's validation, not implementation.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Epic-level: the "aimgr not installed" bootstrap path needs explicit guidance — not just prerequisite detection

**What**: The epic mentions aimgr as the "standard installation path" and says equivalent manual installation should work. But the bootstrap flow (md6.2) does not describe what happens when a user starts Phase 1 with no aimgr and no interest in installing it. The current init template says: "Inform the user: 'aimgr is not installed. You can install it from [link]'" — and then continues. But the resource-backed Phase 2 assumes aimgr-installed resources. If the user manually copies resources, how do they know which files to copy and where?

**Why**: Without aimgr, the only way to reach Phase 2 is to manually create the correct directory structure (`.opencode/skills/opencode-coder/SKILL.md`, `.opencode/commands/opencode-coder/*.md`, `.opencode/agents/*.md`). The bootstrap should either (a) guide the user through manual copying with explicit paths, or (b) point to documentation that explains the manual path. Currently, neither the epic nor any task addresses this.

**Suggested action**: Add to md6.2's bootstrap template instructions: when aimgr is not installed and the user declines to install it, the bootstrap should explain the manual alternative with enough specificity that a user can actually do it. At minimum: "Copy the opencode-coder resource files to `.opencode/` in the expected layout, or install aimgr later and run `aimgr install package/opencode-coder`."

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Critical review summary — plan quality verdict

**Overall**: The epic's direction is correct and the architectural split is well-motivated. The plan is NOT yet safe to implement as-is. There are 5 structural gaps that will cause implementation ambiguity or rework.

### Verdict on the user's 5 highlighted concerns:

**1. Is it clear what must exist for Phase 2?**
NO. md6.1 says "identify the well-known resources" but does not enumerate them. The implementer must choose between using `aimgr verify` (coarse, conflates unrelated resources), file-existence checks (specific but needs an explicit file list), or package declaration checks (easy but doesn't verify actual files). This is the foundational decision and it is currently left entirely open. See comments on md6.1.

**2. Is it clear how the plugin should guide the user in Phase 1, especially with aimgr?**
PARTIALLY. md6.2 lists prerequisite detection and installation guidance as Phase 1 concerns. But it does not explicitly include mode selection (stealth/team/inactive), which MUST happen in Phase 1 for the activation flow to work. It also does not classify beads initialization or mode transitions as Phase 1 or Phase 2. See comments on md6.2.

**3. Is there a clear plan for when aimgr is not installed?**
NO. The epic mentions manual installation as acceptable but never defines what it looks like. The bootstrap template should guide users who lack aimgr toward either installing it or manually copying resources, but no task specifies the manual copy path with enough detail to be useful. See comments on md6 and md6.1.

**4. Do we need to ask for mode in Phase 1?**
YES, we do, and NO, this is not captured. Mode selection is a prerequisite for activation, which is a prerequisite for aimgr auto-install, which is a prerequisite for Phase 2. md6.2 does not list mode selection as a bootstrap concern. This is a gap. See comment on md6.2.

**5. Will all important flows still work?**
NOT WITHOUT FIXING THE INIT COMMAND COLLISION. The `/opencode-coder/init` command is currently always registered by the runtime. In Phase 2, the resource-backed `init.md` wants to provide the same command. No task addresses which one wins. If the runtime always overrides, Phase 2 init behavior is broken. No task or acceptance criterion covers this. See comments on md6, md6.3, and md6.5.

### Summary of issues by task:

| Task | Issue count | Severity |
|------|------------|----------|
| md6 (epic) | 5 issues | 2 critical (init collision, aimgr-absent path), 2 moderate (ecosystemReady interaction, stealth AGENTS injection), 1 simplification |
| md6.1 | 4 issues | 2 critical (no resource list, no manual-install definition), 2 moderate (no return type, no sub-state distinction) |
| md6.2 | 4 issues | 2 critical (mode selection missing, handoff mechanism unclear), 2 moderate (vague acceptance criteria, beads init unclassified) |
| md6.3 | 2 issues | 1 critical (init command dual existence), 1 moderate (gating logic after removal) |
| md6.4 | 2 issues | 1 moderate (test scenarios too generic), 1 minor (same-session handoff testability) |
| md6.5 | 1 issue | 1 critical (missing init handover acceptance criterion) |

### Top 3 recommendations before implementation:

1. **Define the Phase 2 resource contract explicitly in md6.1** with a list of specific files/paths that must exist
2. **Specify the init command lifecycle** across Phase 1 and Phase 2 — who registers it, who wins when both exist
3. **Add mode selection as an explicit Phase 1 bootstrap concern** in md6.2

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Re-review: Init command collision — RESOLVED in notes across tasks

**What**: The previous review's critical finding was that no task addressed the runtime vs resource-backed init collision. This is now resolved. The epic notes state: "`/opencode-coder/init` intentionally has two forms." md6.3 notes state: "runtime init exists only for Phase 1 bootstrap; once Phase 2 resources are available, normal init behavior must come from the resource-backed markdown command." md6.5 notes include verification of this behavior.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Re-review: ecosystemReady interaction — still unaddressed

**What**: The previous review raised a moderate concern about whether the Phase 2 classification changes the semantics of `ecosystemReady`, which currently gates the `default_agent = "orchestrator"` decision. No task or note addresses this.

The current `deriveEcosystemReady()` requires: git initialized + beads initialized + aimgr installed + packageYaml exists + resourcesHealthy. If Phase 2 detection adds new requirements (e.g., skill file existence), and those are layered into `ecosystemReady`, the orchestrator default_agent behavior changes as a side effect for projects that currently pass `ecosystemReady` but lack the specific skill file.

**Why**: This is a regression risk. If `ecosystemReady` is reused as the Phase 2 signal, its meaning changes. If Phase 2 is a separate concept, `ecosystemReady` is unaffected. No task states which approach to use.

**Suggested action**: Add one sentence to md6.1 notes: "Phase 2 classification must be a separate concept from `ecosystemReady`. The `ecosystemReady` flag and its consumers (default_agent gating) must not change behavior as a result of this epic." This is a low-effort clarification that prevents a subtle regression.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Re-review: Stealth mode AGENTS.md injection — still unaddressed but low risk

**What**: The previous review noted that the stealth mode `.coder/AGENTS.md` injection in `src/index.ts` lines 229-238 is operational runtime logic that could be accidentally removed during md6.3's "remove hardcoded normal-operation workflow text" sweep. No task or note mentions this explicitly.

**Why**: The risk is real but the likelihood is low. The injection code is clearly structural (it reads a file path and pushes it to `input.instructions`), not a template string. An implementer reading "remove hardcoded workflow text" would likely not misidentify a 4-line file-existence check as workflow text. But the previous review's point stands: the boundary between "operational runtime logic" and "workflow text" is not documented.

**Suggested action**: This is a nice-to-have. Add a code comment near the AGENTS.md injection block: `// Operational runtime logic — survives the bootstrap/normal-operation refactor`. Or mention it in md6.3 notes. Low priority.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Re-review: Task consolidation (md6.2 + md6.3 merge) — still valid but not blocking

**What**: The previous review suggested merging md6.2 (bootstrap init) and md6.3 (remove hardcoded prompts) into a single task because they are tightly coupled — both modify `src/index.ts`, both depend on md6.1, and the init command lifecycle spans both.

With the notes now clarifying the init command lifecycle, the coupling is less dangerous because the design decisions are documented rather than left to each implementer independently. But the tasks still modify the same code in complementary ways.

**Why**: The risk of conflicting intermediate states is reduced but not eliminated. If a single agent implements md6.2 and md6.3 back-to-back (which is the likely flow), the coupling is manageable. If different agents implement them in parallel, there will be merge conflicts in `src/index.ts`.

**Suggested action**: Keep as-is if a single agent will implement both sequentially. Consider merging if parallel implementation is planned. This is no longer a structural risk — it's an operational preference.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Re-review: aimgr-not-installed bootstrap path — PARTIALLY resolved

**What**: The previous review flagged that the "aimgr not installed" path lacked guidance for manual resource installation. The md6.2 notes now say: "If aimgr is not installed, explicitly guide the user through the standard aimgr install path and also define the manual-install alternative for commands, skills, and agents if they do not want to use aimgr."

This addresses the concern at the task level. The bootstrap template is now required to offer both the aimgr install path AND a manual alternative.

The remaining gap: the md6.1 resource contract says to "accept equivalent manual installation" but never defines what manual installation means at the file level (which files go where). The md6.2 notes say "define the manual-install alternative" but don't specify it. The implementer of the bootstrap template needs to know which files to tell the user to copy and where.

**Why**: The bootstrap template will need to say something like "copy these files to these paths." Without a defined file list, the implementer will have to reverse-engineer the resource layout from the aimgr package definition.

**Suggested action**: This is now a minor gap rather than a critical one. The resource list in md6.1's notes (skill/opencode-coder, 7 commands, agents) combined with the standard `.opencode/` directory layout gives the implementer enough to derive the file paths. But spelling out the target paths (`.opencode/skills/opencode-coder/SKILL.md`, `.opencode/commands/opencode-coder/*.md`, `.opencode/agents/*.md`) in the bootstrap template spec would eliminate all guesswork.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Re-review verdict: SAFE TO IMPLEMENT with 2 moderate and 3 minor gaps remaining

**Overall**: The epic and its tasks have been substantially improved since the first review. All 5 previous critical findings are resolved. The plan is now safe to implement. The remaining gaps are moderate-to-minor and will not cause structural rework — they may cause small implementation questions that a competent tasker can resolve inline.

### Status of the 6 user-requested review points:

**1. Is it now clear what must exist for Phase 2? Is the resource contract precise enough?**
YES — with one moderate residual. The notes enumerate specific resources (skill, 7 commands, agents). Detection uses "actual available resource surfaces/paths." The phase-classification result type is specified. The one gap: the agent requirement decision ("must all 4 agents be present?") is asked but not answered. This is moderate because it affects the Phase 2 boundary definition, but the simplest answer (decouple agents from Phase 2, check them separately for orchestrator) is obvious.

**2. Is it now clear how the plugin should guide the user in Phase 1, including interactive prompting?**
YES. The notes specify: ask for mode, offer aimgr install when available, define manual-install alternative when aimgr is absent. Phase 1 is interactive (not just instructions). Package install prompting via `question()` is called out.

**3. Is there now a clear plan for when aimgr is not installed?**
YES — with one minor residual. The notes say "guide the user through the standard aimgr install path and also define the manual-install alternative." The minor gap: the exact file paths for manual installation are not listed, but they are derivable from the resource contract in md6.1.

**4. Is it now clear that mode selection/preservation must be handled in Phase 1?**
YES. The epic notes and md6.2 notes both explicitly state this. This was the clearest improvement from the first review.

**5. Is the `/opencode-coder/init` Phase 1 vs Phase 2 split now intentional and sufficiently specified?**
YES. The epic notes say init "intentionally has two forms." md6.3 notes say "runtime init exists only for Phase 1 bootstrap; once Phase 2 resources are available, normal init behavior must come from the resource-backed markdown command." md6.5 notes verify this. The restart-based handoff (not same-session) is specified. One minor contradiction: the md6.2 description still says "same session" while the notes say "restart" — the notes take precedence and the description should be cleaned up.

**6. Will all important plugin use cases and flows still work?**
YES — with one moderate gap. The `ecosystemReady` / `default_agent` interaction is not addressed: if Phase 2 detection changes `ecosystemReady` semantics, the orchestrator behavior changes. The fix is simple (keep Phase 2 classification separate from `ecosystemReady`), but it needs to be stated. The stealth AGENTS.md injection, disabled mode, and command suppression logic are all implicitly preserved but the boundary between "operational runtime logic" and "workflow text" is not documented — low risk, easily mitigated with a code comment.

### Remaining issues grouped by task:

| Task | Issue | Severity | Action |
|------|-------|----------|--------|
| md6.1 | Agent presence requirement undecided | MODERATE | Decide: agents not required for Phase 2, checked separately for orchestrator |
| md6.1 | Detection mechanism wording slightly ambiguous | MINOR | Add one sentence naming the primary file-existence signal |
| md6.2 | Description contradicts notes on same-session vs restart handoff | MINOR | Update description to match restart-based notes |
| md6.2 | Beads init / mode transitions not classified as Phase 1 or Phase 2 | MODERATE | Decide and state (recommend: Phase 2 skill-backed) |
| md6.2 | "Behaves sensibly" acceptance criterion still vague | MINOR | Nice-to-have: replace with concrete expectations |
| md6.3 | Suppression/deletion logic survival not explicitly stated | MINOR | Add one sentence to notes |
| md6 (epic) | ecosystemReady interaction unaddressed | MODERATE | Add one sentence: Phase 2 is separate from ecosystemReady |
| md6 (epic) | Stealth AGENTS.md injection not mentioned | MINOR | Add a code comment or note |

### Verdict: SAFE

The plan is safe to implement. The 2 moderate gaps (agent requirement decision, beads-init Phase classification) will cause the implementer to pause and make a judgment call, but the intent is clear enough that the right judgment call is obvious. The 3 minor gaps are cosmetic or preventive. None of them will cause structural rework.

**Ready for tasker implementation**: YES — with the recommendation to resolve the 2 moderate gaps before starting (they are quick decisions, not design work).

title: Define resource contract and phase detection for plugin bootstrap
description:
## Description
Define the runtime contract for which opencode-coder resources the plugin expects and how it decides whether it is operating in Phase 1 bootstrap or Phase 2 normal operation.

## Instructions
1. Identify the well-known resources the plugin expects for full Phase 2 operation, including the relevant commands, skill, and agent surfaces.
2. Treat aimgr plus the opencode-coder package as the standard installation path, but make the detection logic accept equivalent manual installation or copied resources as valid too.
3. Update the runtime detection logic so it can classify the project/session as:
   - Phase 1 bootstrap: resources required for normal operation are not sufficiently available
   - Phase 2 normal operation: the required resource surfaces are available
4. Keep the classification logic explicit enough that other runtime code can register/gate commands without embedding workflow instructions.
5. Record the bootstrap-vs-normal-operation assumptions in the relevant runtime code or nearby comments so the architecture is understandable from the implementation.

## Files to Modify
- src/index.ts — consume phase classification for command registration/gating
- src/service/project-detector-service.ts — define or expose the resource/phase detection inputs if needed
- src/service/aimgr-service.ts — contribute resource availability signals if needed
- other runtime support files in src/service/ or src/core/ only if needed to make the classification explicit

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The plugin has an explicit notion of Phase 1 bootstrap vs Phase 2 normal operation
- [ ] Full-operation resource expectations are defined clearly enough for runtime gating
- [ ] Equivalent manual resource installation is accepted, not only aimgr package installation
- [ ] The runtime classification is understandable without embedding command workflow prose in code
close_reason: Implemented and verified as part of phase split work

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## No enumerated list of required resources for Phase 2

**What**: The task says "Identify the well-known resources the plugin expects for full Phase 2 operation, including the relevant commands, skill, and agent surfaces" but does not define them. The acceptance criteria say "Full-operation resource expectations are defined clearly enough for runtime gating" — but the task leaves it entirely to the implementer to decide what those resources are. There is no seed list.

**Why**: This is the single most important decision in the entire epic. The phase classification is only as good as its resource contract. Right now, the existing `resourcesHealthy` check delegates to `aimgr verify --format json` which checks *all* declared resources in `ai.package.yaml` — but that file is project-specific and varies across installations. There is no mechanism today to say "specifically these resources from the opencode-coder package must be present." Without an explicit list, the implementer could:
- (A) keep using `aimgr verify` as a coarse proxy, which conflates opencode-coder resources with unrelated declared resources
- (B) check for specific file paths (`.opencode/commands/opencode-coder/*.md`, `.opencode/skills/opencode-coder/SKILL.md`, `.opencode/agents/*.md`)
- (C) check for the `package/opencode-coder` declaration in `ai.package.yaml` only

Each gives a different Phase 2 boundary. The task must pick one or explain the tradeoff.

**Suggested action**: Add an explicit seed list to the instructions. Based on `opencode-coder.package.json`, the minimum Phase 2 contract is likely:
- The `opencode-coder` skill is loadable (`.opencode/skills/opencode-coder/SKILL.md` exists)
- The `opencode-coder/init` command resource exists (`.opencode/commands/opencode-coder/init.md`)
- At least one agent is available (`.opencode/agents/orchestrator.md` at minimum)

Then state whether `aimgr verify` healthy is still an additional requirement or whether file-existence checks alone are sufficient.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## "Equivalent manual installation" is accepted but never defined

**What**: Acceptance criterion says "Equivalent manual resource installation is accepted, not only aimgr package installation." The instructions say "make the detection logic accept equivalent manual installation or copied resources as valid too." But neither defines what manual installation looks like in practice.

**Why**: If the implementer checks `aimgr verify` as the Phase 2 gate, manually-copied files will fail verification because they are not tracked in `ai.package.yaml`. If the implementer checks file paths instead, they need to know which exact files must exist. The instruction "accept equivalent manual installation" is not actionable without specifying the detection strategy: file-existence checks? A combination of file checks plus optional `aimgr verify`? Something else?

**Suggested action**: Specify the detection strategy explicitly. The simplest approach: check for the existence of the `opencode-coder` skill file (`.opencode/skills/opencode-coder/SKILL.md`) as the primary Phase 2 signal. This works for both aimgr-installed and manually-copied resources. Then optionally layer `aimgr verify` on top for richer health reporting. State this decision in the task so the implementer does not have to invent it.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Phase classification lacks a defined return type or data structure

**What**: The task says "Update the runtime detection logic so it can classify the project/session as Phase 1 bootstrap or Phase 2 normal operation" and "Keep the classification logic explicit enough that other runtime code can register/gate commands without embedding workflow instructions." But it does not specify the shape of the classification output — is it a boolean? An enum? A new field on `ProjectContext`? A new service?

**Why**: This matters because `src/index.ts` currently consumes `ProjectContext.aimgr.resourcesHealthy` and `ProjectContext.ecosystemReady` for gating. If the new phase classification is a separate concept, the implementer needs to know where it lives and how other code consumes it. If it maps onto the existing `ecosystemReady` flag, say that explicitly. If it's a new `phase: "bootstrap" | "normal"` field on `ProjectContext`, say that. Without this, the implementer will invent a structure that may or may not integrate cleanly.

**Suggested action**: State explicitly whether the phase classification is:
- A new field on `ProjectContext` (e.g. `phase: "bootstrap" | "normal"`)
- A standalone function/service
- A reinterpretation of existing `ecosystemReady` + `resourcesHealthy`

The first option is simplest and most consistent with the existing code.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## The aimgr-not-installed case is under-specified for Phase 1 bootstrap

**What**: The current code already handles `aimgr.installed === false` at the `ProjectContext` level, but md6.1 does not describe what the Phase 1 bootstrap should look like when aimgr is absent vs. when aimgr is present but resources are missing. These are different Phase 1 states that require different bootstrap guidance.

**Why**: When aimgr is installed but resources are missing, the bootstrap can offer `aimgr install package/opencode-coder`. When aimgr is NOT installed, the bootstrap must either guide the user to install aimgr first, or offer a manual resource-copy path. The current init template handles this distinction (it has separate sections for "aimgr not installed" vs "opencode-coder package not installed"), but the phase classification task says nothing about whether these sub-states matter for the classification or whether they are just UI concerns for md6.2.

**Suggested action**: Clarify whether Phase 1 has sub-states (aimgr-absent vs aimgr-present-but-resources-missing) or whether they are treated as one undifferentiated "bootstrap" state. If sub-states exist, they should be part of the classification output so md6.2 can consume them cleanly.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Re-review: Resource contract is now substantially specified in notes — one gap remains

**What**: The notes now enumerate the minimum resource surfaces for Phase 2 (skill/opencode-coder, 7 command resources, agent resources). They also specify that the detection mechanism should use "actual available resource surfaces/paths rather than only aimgr state or package declarations." This directly addresses the previous review's critical finding that no resource list existed. The notes also require an explicit phase-classification result type with `current phase, missing resources, aimgr available, package installed, bootstrap-init-vs-resource-backed-commands`.

The remaining gap: the notes say "explicitly decide whether orchestrator, tasker, reviewer, and verifier must all be present" but do not actually make that decision. The implementer still has to choose. For the skill and command surfaces the list is explicit, but for agents it is still a question mark.

**Why**: Agent presence determines whether the orchestrator default_agent logic works correctly. If Phase 2 requires all 4 agents but only 3 are installed, the classification fails to Phase 1 — and the user sees bootstrap init instead of normal init on a project that is 95% ready. This is a UX cliff. Conversely, if Phase 2 does not require agents at all, the orchestrator may be set as default_agent even when its definition file does not exist, causing a broken orchestrator flow.

**Suggested action**: Make the agent decision now. The simplest correct answer: Phase 2 requires the opencode-coder skill + the init command resource. Agent presence is checked separately for the `default_agent = "orchestrator"` decision (which already has its own `ecosystemReady` gate). This avoids coupling the phase classification to agent availability, which is the current concern about `ecosystemReady` semantics changing.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Re-review: Detection mechanism still slightly ambiguous — downgraded from CRITICAL to MINOR

**What**: The notes say "Define the detection mechanism using actual available resource surfaces/paths rather than only aimgr state or package declarations." This sounds like file-existence checks but doesn't fully commit. The previous review asked: is it file-existence checks, aimgr verify, or a combination? The notes lean toward file-existence but use descriptive rather than prescriptive language.

**Why**: The implementer needs a concrete decision. The phrase "actual available resource surfaces/paths" is 80% of the way to saying "check file existence," and a competent implementer will get there. This is no longer a blocking gap but remains a source of potential misinterpretation.

**Suggested action**: Adding one sentence would eliminate all ambiguity: "The primary Phase 2 signal is the existence of `.opencode/skills/opencode-coder/SKILL.md`; all other signals are supplementary." This is now a nice-to-have, not a blocker.

title: OpenCode primitive gap: headless skill-trigger eval automation for skill-creator
description: Discovered while working on opencode-coder-a1p.2. The upstream skill-creator description optimization pipeline relies on nested  subprocess runs, temporary  injection, and stream-json tool events to detect Skill/Read usage. OpenCode currently lacks an equivalent non-interactive primitive for (1) launching isolated runs from scripts, (2) injecting ephemeral skills per run, and (3) retrieving structured tool-use events for trigger-rate measurement. Track implementation of an OpenCode-native replacement or explicit API contract so scripts/run_eval.py and scripts/run_loop.py can be re-enabled.
close_reason: Superseded by the implemented OpenCode-native trigger-eval and description-optimization replacement in scripts/run_eval.py, scripts/improve_description.py, and scripts/run_loop.py; remaining concern is signal/API hardening, not a blocker that prevents the workflow from running.

## Proposed mandate and acceptance criteria for the upstream-preserving realignment

**What**: This task should be the primary implementation task for the new "minimal port" direction. Here are the exact acceptance criteria I recommend:

### Acceptance Criteria for a1p.8

**Upstream preservation gate:**
- [ ] The ported SKILL.md starts from a verbatim copy of the upstream `.opencode/skills/skill-creator/SKILL.md`
- [ ] Every change from upstream is one of: (a) Claude-specific incompatibility fix, (b) new OpenCode-specific addition, or (c) intentional content change with inline rationale comment

- [ ] The upstream's conversational/pedagogical tone is preserved in generic sections — do not convert personality-rich prose to bullet lists

**Claude-specific content that MUST be changed:**
- [ ] All references to `claude -p`, `claude` CLI, Claude Code session model → replaced with OpenCode equivalents or marked as deferred
- [ ] "Spawn two subagents in the same turn" → replaced with OpenCode-compatible execution guidance (serial with clear labeling, or parallel if available)
- [ ] "you receive a notification containing total_tokens and duration_ms" → replaced with the fallback capture approach from the current port (it's good)
- [ ] "Claude.ai-specific instructions" section → removed entirely (not applicable to OpenCode)
- [ ] "Cowork-Specific Instructions" section → removed entirely (not applicable to OpenCode)
- [ ] "run claude-with-access-to-the-skill" → replaced with OpenCode skill-loading equivalent
- [ ] "Please add steps to your TodoList" → removed (TodoList is Claude Code-specific)
- [ ] "present_files" tool references → replaced with OpenCode file presentation
- [ ] `~/Downloads` assumptions → replaced with explicit path handling
- [ ] YAML frontmatter `name` and `description` → updated for opencode-coder-skill-creator identity

**OpenCode-specific additions to graft in (from current port):**
- [ ] "OpenCode Environment Assumptions" section — add as new section, do not replace existing content
- [ ] "Agent Mapping (OpenCode)" section — add as new section with the standard workflow role mapping and bundled instruction-file mapping
- [ ] "Model Selection Guidance" section — add as new section
- [ ] Timing capture fallback hierarchy (from current port Step 3) — replace upstream Step 3 in-place
- [ ] Headless/no-browser fallback guidance — add to viewer sections, do not remove browser-available paths

**Structural rules:**
- [ ] Preserve upstream section ordering and naming where possible — do not reorganize sections that don't need reorganization
- [ ] If a section is split or reorganized, document why in the PR
- [ ] Do not add a `render_eval_review.py` helper script — the upstream inline approach (agent reads template, substitutes placeholders, writes file) is correct and simpler
- [ ] The final document should be 450-520 lines (upstream is 485 lines; additions should roughly offset removals)

**Why**: These criteria enforce both sides of the policy: no Claude-specific incompatibilities remain, AND no generic upstream content was unnecessarily changed or lost.

**Suggested action**: Replace the current empty a1p.8 description with these criteria and remove the `needs:discussion` label.

title: Restructure opencode-coder skill as the command workflow hub
description:
## Description
Restructure `ai-resources/skills/opencode-coder/` so it becomes the canonical workflow hub behind the `opencode-coder` command set. This task owns the top-level skill structure: supported use cases, routing, argument expectations, and the split between `SKILL.md` and detailed reference files.

## Instructions
1. Audit the current `opencode-coder` skill and references against the command set under `ai-resources/commands/opencode-coder/`.
2. Define a clean top-level structure in `ai-resources/skills/opencode-coder/SKILL.md` that explains which supported workflows the skill owns and which reference file is the source of truth for each workflow.
3. Make sure the skill, not the commands, owns the reusable content for:
   - when a workflow is appropriate
   - supported use cases
   - argument expectations and any meaningful free-text inputs
   - workflow routing to detailed references
4. Reorganize or add references where needed so the detailed logic is discoverable without bloating `SKILL.md`.
5. Keep the final structure concise and explicit enough that the command tasks can slim down to lightweight shortcuts.

## Files to Modify
- ai-resources/skills/opencode-coder/SKILL.md — define the command-backed workflow map and supported-use-case structure
- ai-resources/skills/opencode-coder/references/** — reorganize or add reference docs so detailed workflows live outside command entry files

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `SKILL.md` clearly maps each command-backed workflow to a source-of-truth reference or section
- [ ] Supported use cases and argument expectations are described in the skill layer instead of being stranded in commands
- [ ] The skill/reference split is clear enough that command entry files can become thin wrappers without losing workflow clarity
- [ ] The resulting structure is concise and navigable rather than a monolithic command dump

title: Refactor opencode-coder commands into thin skill wrappers
description:
## Description
Refactor the `opencode-coder` slash commands so commands are lightweight user entrypoints and the reusable workflow logic lives in the `opencode-coder` skill and its references. The skill should become the canonical home for supported use cases, workflow routing, argument expectations, and detailed procedures.

## Goals

- Keep each command as a thin user shortcut that quickly routes into a skill-backed workflow
- Make supported use cases and argument contracts explicit in the skill

- Leave the `opencode-coder` skill with a clean, discoverable structure that maps command names to the right workflow references

## Success Criteria
