title: Collapse user-facing diagnostics to treat opencode-coder as a single installable resource
description:
## Description
Bootstrap install diagnostics and runtime project context currently leak low-level opencode-coder internals by enumerating command/reference surfaces and `skill-reference/opencode-coder/...` entries. Users should see opencode-coder as one installable resource, not a collection of individual files.

The user-facing contract should treat the `opencode-coder` skill/resource as a single entity, using `.opencode/skills/opencode-coder/SKILL.md` as the concrete marker for whether that resource is present. Internal per-file checks may still exist for classification or degraded-mode detection, but that detail must not appear in bootstrap guidance or runtime project context.

## Instructions
1. Update bootstrap/manual install guidance so it tells users to install the `opencode-coder` skill/resources as one unit instead of listing every command and reference file.
2. Preserve a usable manual-install path for environments without `aimgr`; if needed, describe the resource at directory/skill level with `SKILL.md` as the presence marker.
3. Change runtime/project-context diagnostics so exposed required surfaces collapse to a high-level `opencode-coder` resource signal rather than per-file `skill-reference/...` or `command/opencode-coder/...` entries.
4. Keep detailed per-file checks internal only if they are still required for detection/classification.
5. Review optional-agent/related diagnostics for consistency so user-visible status does not mix flattened required surfaces with low-level file listings elsewhere.
6. Update unit/integration tests and fixtures to match the new single-entity diagnostics contract.

## Files to Modify
- src/templates/init-install-guide.ts — collapse bootstrap guidance to a single opencode-coder resource
- src/service/project-detector-service.ts — expose high-level runtime/project-context diagnostics
- tests/unit/service/project-detector-service.test.ts — update runtime classification expectations and helper fixtures
- tests/integration/plugin.test.ts — update project-context assertions/fixtures that reference required surfaces

## Expected Behavior
- Bootstrap diagnostics describe `opencode-coder` as one installable skill/resource.
- Runtime project context reports the high-level opencode-coder resource state instead of enumerating `skill-reference/opencode-coder/...` and related command surfaces.
- `.opencode/skills/opencode-coder/SKILL.md` is the concrete user-facing marker for the resource.
- Internal completeness checks may remain granular, but users and agents do not see those low-level file inventories in diagnostics.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Bootstrap/manual install guidance references only the `opencode-coder` skill/resource as the install unit
- [ ] User-visible runtime/project-context diagnostics no longer expose `skill-reference/opencode-coder/...` entries
- [ ] User-visible runtime/project-context diagnostics no longer expose per-file `command/opencode-coder/...` entries for this resource
- [ ] `.opencode/skills/opencode-coder/SKILL.md` is used as the concrete marker for user-facing resource presence messaging
- [ ] Bootstrap detection still degrades correctly when the opencode-coder resource is incomplete or unavailable
- [ ] Unit and integration tests are updated and pass for the changed diagnostics contract

## Risks / Notes
- Changing exposed runtime diagnostics may require adjusting any TypeScript interfaces or tests that currently assume per-surface keys.
- Avoid removing internal file-level validation if it is still needed to distinguish healthy vs degraded bootstrap states.
close_reason: Implemented and verified: user-facing diagnostics now treat opencode-coder as a single installable resource; targeted tests, e2e scenarios, typecheck, and build passed.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Title is misleading — this is about hiding internal resource granularity, not about "the skill"

**What**: The current title "Simplify bootstrap install diagnostics to report only the opencode-coder skill" implies the fix is to tell users about a single skill file. But the actual problem spans three distinct surfaces: (1) the bootstrap install template enumerating 20+ individual files, (2) `project.yaml` exposing per-file `requiredSurfaceAvailability` entries, and (3) `missingRequiredSurfaces` leaking `skill-reference/opencode-coder/...` paths to consumers. The word "skill" in the title is ambiguous — it could mean the SKILL.md file, the skill resource, or the aimgr package.

**Why**: A tasker reading this title will think the fix is about replacing file lists with a reference to SKILL.md. But the actual intent (per user clarification) is that `opencode-coder` should be treated as ONE installable entity across all user-facing surfaces. The title needs to convey that this is about abstraction level, not about a specific file.

**Suggested action**: Rename to: `Collapse user-facing diagnostics to treat opencode-coder as a single installable resource`

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Description conflates two separate problems that need distinct treatment

**What**: The description mixes two concerns as if they're one fix: (A) the bootstrap install template listing individual files to a human user (lines 52-55 of init-install-guide.ts), and (B) the project.yaml runtime context exposing per-file `requiredSurfaceAvailability` and `missingRequiredSurfaces` entries to the AI agent. These are different audiences with different needs. The template problem is about user-facing messaging. The project.yaml problem is about what the AI agent (and potentially other consumers) sees in structured context.

**Why**: A tasker might apply the same solution to both — e.g., just replacing file lists with "install opencode-coder" everywhere. But the project.yaml case is more nuanced. The AI agent consuming project.yaml may still need to know whether the problem is missing commands vs. missing skill vs. missing references to give useful guidance. Flattening too aggressively in project.yaml could break the agent's ability to diagnose partial installs.

**Suggested action**: Split the description into two clearly labeled sections:
1. **User-facing template**: Replace file enumeration with a single "install the opencode-coder skill/resource" message, with `.opencode/skills/opencode-coder/SKILL.md` as the existence marker.
2. **Agent-facing project.yaml**: Collapse `requiredSurfaceAvailability` from 20+ individual entries to category-level entries (e.g., `commands: true/false`, `skill: true/false`, `references: true/false`), and collapse `missingRequiredSurfaces` to category names rather than individual file paths. Keep per-file checks internal to `classifyRuntimePhase()`.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Acceptance criterion #2 is underspecified — what replaces the per-file entries?

**What**: Criterion #2 says "`.coder/project.yaml` runtime phase no longer exposes `skill-reference/opencode-coder/...` entries" — but it only mentions skill-reference entries. The same problem applies to the 7 `command/opencode-coder/*` entries in `requiredSurfaceAvailability`. And it says nothing about what the replacement structure should look like.

**Why**: Without specifying the target structure, a tasker could: (a) remove `requiredSurfaceAvailability` entirely (losing diagnostic value), (b) replace it with a single boolean (too coarse for the agent), or (c) keep commands but remove references (inconsistent). The acceptance criteria should define the expected output format.

**Suggested action**: Replace criterion #2 with:
- `.coder/project.yaml` `requiredSurfaceAvailability` uses category-level keys (`commands`, `skill`, `references`) instead of per-file paths
- `missingRequiredSurfaces` reports category names (e.g., `references`) rather than individual file paths like `skill-reference/opencode-coder/status-health.md`
- `optionalAgentAvailability` follows the same pattern if it's user/agent-visible

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## TypeScript interface change is a breaking contract — `RuntimePhaseClassification` is exported

**What**: The `RuntimePhaseClassification` interface is exported from `project-detector-service.ts` and its `requiredSurfaceAvailability` field is typed as `Record<string, boolean>`. Changing the keys from per-file paths to category-level names is a breaking change for any code that pattern-matches on keys like `"skill-reference/opencode-coder/..."` or `"command/opencode-coder/init"`. The integration tests already assert on specific key names (e.g., `plugin.test.ts` lines 17-37, 404-406). The `missingRequiredSurfaces` array type stays `string[]` but the semantics change (from paths to categories).

**Why**: If there are consumers outside the test files that depend on these keys, this is a breaking API change. Even within this repo, the integration test fixtures are extensive — at least 6 test cases construct `requiredSurfaceAvailability` with per-file keys. The bug description lists only 4 files to modify, but the fixture helper `createProjectContext()` appears in both test files and will need updating.

**Suggested action**: Add to the instructions: "This changes the shape of `RuntimePhaseClassification.requiredSurfaceAvailability` and `missingRequiredSurfaces`. Verify no external consumers depend on per-file keys. Update the `createProjectContextFixture()` helper in both unit and integration test files."

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Bootstrap template manual path still needs SOME file guidance — zero detail is also wrong

**What**: The description says to stop printing the full command/reference file inventory in the bootstrap template. But the manual install path (lines 51-55 of init-install-guide.ts) exists specifically for users who cannot use aimgr. If we remove all file detail, a user doing manual install has no idea what to copy. The bug frames this as "don't enumerate files" but the user clarification says "reference it as one entity" — these are in tension for the manual path.

**Why**: The manual install path is a real use case. A user who can't install aimgr needs to know what to put where. Telling them "install the opencode-coder skill" is useless without aimgr. The fix needs to find a middle ground: reference the skill as one entity but still provide actionable manual instructions.

**Suggested action**: For the manual path, replace the file enumeration with: "Copy the complete `opencode-coder` skill directory to `.opencode/skills/opencode-coder/` (the SKILL.md file is the required marker) and the matching commands to `.opencode/commands/opencode-coder/`. The full file manifest is available in the package repository." This treats it as one entity while still giving enough structure for manual setup. Add this nuance to the instructions.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Missing file: the e2e fixture `project.yaml` will also need updating

**What**: The "Files to Modify" section lists 4 files but omits `tests/e2e/fixtures/existing-active-project/.coder/project.yaml`. This fixture currently has no `runtimePhase` block, so it may not be affected today — but if any e2e test is added that checks project.yaml structure, this fixture becomes stale. More importantly, the integration test helper `createProjectContext()` in `tests/integration/plugin.test.ts` (lines 10-73) and the unit test helper `createProjectContextFixture()` in the unit test (lines 9-61) both construct the full per-file `requiredSurfaceAvailability` and will definitely break.

**Why**: The files-to-modify list should be complete so the tasker doesn't miss test fixtures and get surprised by failures.

**Suggested action**: Add a note under "Files to Modify" that the `createProjectContext()` / `createProjectContextFixture()` helpers in both test files are the primary fixtures to update, and flag the e2e fixture for review.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Simplification opportunity: `optionalAgentAvailability` should get the same treatment

**What**: The bug only mentions collapsing `requiredSurfaceAvailability` and `missingRequiredSurfaces`. But `optionalAgentAvailability` (lines 396-401 of the detector, lines 39-44 of project.yaml) also exposes per-file agent paths like `agent/orchestrator`, `agent/tasker`, etc. If the goal is "one entity, not many files," this field should be collapsed too — e.g., to a single `agents: true/false` or `agentCount: 4`.

**Why**: Leaving `optionalAgentAvailability` at per-file granularity while collapsing `requiredSurfaceAvailability` creates an inconsistent abstraction. The agent reading project.yaml sees categories for required surfaces but individual files for optional ones. This is confusing and will need a follow-up fix.

**Suggested action**: Include `optionalAgentAvailability` in the same collapse. Since agents are optional and the count is small (4), a single boolean `optionalAgentsAvailable: true/false` or a summary like `agents: { available: 4, expected: 4 }` would be sufficient.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Integration test assertion on template content will break — needs explicit criterion

**What**: The integration test at plugin.test.ts line 475 asserts `cfg.command?.["opencode-coder/init"]?.template).toContain("required skill references")`. After this fix, the template won't contain "required skill references" because the manual path will no longer enumerate references. This assertion will fail silently during the fix unless the tasker knows to update it.

**Why**: The test is checking that the bootstrap template provides complete manual guidance. The replacement assertions need to verify the new wording (e.g., "install the opencode-coder skill" or whatever the new phrasing is). Without guidance on what the new phrasing should be, the tasker will invent it, and it may not match the intent.

**Suggested action**: Add to the acceptance criteria: "Integration test assertions on bootstrap template content are updated to verify the new single-entity messaging (not per-file enumeration)." Optionally, provide the expected phrasing for the manual path so test updates are deterministic.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Summary: recommended refined bug specification

After reviewing the code, tests, and current bug framing, here is the tightened specification I recommend:

---

**Recommended title**: `Collapse user-facing diagnostics to treat opencode-coder as a single installable resource`

**Problem statement**: Bootstrap install guidance (init-install-guide.ts) enumerates 20+ individual command/reference/skill files when guiding manual installation. The runtime project context (project.yaml) exposes the same per-file granularity in `requiredSurfaceAvailability` (20 entries), `missingRequiredSurfaces`, and `optionalAgentAvailability` (4 entries). The opencode-coder skill/package is ONE installable entity backed by many files — user-facing and agent-facing diagnostics should reference it at that level. Internal per-file checks for phase classification can stay, but must not leak outward.

**Expected behavior**:
1. Bootstrap template manual path describes opencode-coder as a single resource to install, with `.opencode/skills/opencode-coder/SKILL.md` as the concrete marker, and provides directory-level copy instructions (not file-by-file lists).
2. `project.yaml` `requiredSurfaceAvailability` uses category-level keys (`commands`, `skill`, `references`) with boolean values.
3. `project.yaml` `missingRequiredSurfaces` reports category names, not individual file paths.
4. `project.yaml` `optionalAgentAvailability` follows the same category-level pattern.
5. Internal `classifyRuntimePhase()` retains per-file checks for accurate phase detection.

**Recommended acceptance criteria**:
- [ ] Bootstrap install guidance references opencode-coder as a single installable resource, not individual files
- [ ] Manual install path provides directory-level copy instructions with SKILL.md as the existence marker
- [ ] `requiredSurfaceAvailability` in project.yaml uses category-level keys, not per-file paths
- [ ] `missingRequiredSurfaces` reports categories, not individual file paths
- [ ] `optionalAgentAvailability` follows the same collapse pattern
- [ ] Internal per-file detection logic in `classifyRuntimePhase()` is preserved (not removed)
- [ ] `RuntimePhaseClassification` TypeScript interface updated; no external consumers broken
- [ ] Unit test fixtures (`createProjectContextFixture`), integration test fixtures (`createProjectContext`), and integration test template assertions all updated
- [ ] All unit and integration tests pass

**Risks/ambiguities**:
- The manual install path tension (see separate comment) — removing all file detail breaks manual users, but enumerating files contradicts the "one entity" goal. Needs a middle-ground decision.
- `RuntimePhaseClassification` is an exported interface — verify there are no consumers outside this repo before changing the shape.

title: Increase or document run_loop timeout for representative eval prompts
description:
Discovered while verifying opencode-coder-a1p.9.

## Problem
The documented iterative loop command in SKILL.md omits --timeout, so it uses scripts/run_loop.py default timeout=30. On the current runtime this is too short for the representative skill-creation prompt, producing runner_exception false failures.

## Reproduction
Run:
python3 -m scripts.run_loop --eval-set ai-resources/skills/opencode-coder-workspace/skill-creator-parity-eval/eval-set-representative.json --skill-path ai-resources/skills/opencode-coder-skill-creator --description "Use this skill only when the user asks to create a new skill from scratch. Do not use it for edits, reviews, evaluation workflows, or packaging." --max-iterations 2 --runs-per-query 1 --holdout 0 --results-dir /tmp/skill-creator-verify-run-loop --report none --verbose

Observed result: query-000 timed out after 30 seconds in both iterations and the loop stopped at 2/4.

## Evidence
- scripts/run_loop.py default timeout is 30 seconds.
- The recorded loop output under /tmp/skill-creator-verify-run-loop/... contains runner_exception entries for query-000.
- A direct run_eval invocation with the higher default timeout (120s) completed the same prompt, showing the loop default is the limiting factor.

## Impact
The documented CLI-only improvement loop is not reliably runnable on the representative parity eval set with current defaults.
close_reason: Updated run_loop default timeout to 120s and documented --timeout 120 in SKILL.md iterative loop example; validated representative parity run_loop now completes without 30s runner_exception timeout.

title: Found: inline eval-review template remains vulnerable to </script> injection
description:
Discovered while re-verifying opencode-coder-a1p.8 after the helper-script removal.

The documented upstream-style eval-review flow in ai-resources/skills/opencode-coder-skill-creator/SKILL.md now tells the agent to read assets/eval_review.html and replace __EVAL_DATA_PLACEHOLDER__ with the raw JSON array of eval items in a JS variable assignment. However, assets/eval_review.html embeds that replacement inside an inline <script> block:

const EVAL_DATA = __EVAL_DATA_PLACEHOLDER__;

If an eval query contains </script><script>..., direct JSON insertion breaks out of the script block and can inject extra script tags or break the page. Repro used during verification: substitute JSON containing {"query": "</script><script>alert(1)</script>", "should_trigger": true} into the template; the rendered HTML contains the literal closing script tag inside the inline script.

Why this matters: the provisional helper-script XSS bug was removed with render_eval_review.py, but the same underlying safety issue still exists in the current documented inline workflow and template.
close_reason: Hardened eval review template against </script> breakout by switching to decodeURIComponent+JSON.parse placeholder flow and updated SKILL.md replacement instructions accordingly.

title: OpenCode skill-creator manual eval-review flow is not actionable
description: Discovered while verifying opencode-coder-a1p.5. The rewritten SKILL.md says to use assets/eval_review.html for trigger-description review, but it no longer documents the required placeholder substitution/render step. The raw asset still contains __EVAL_DATA_PLACEHOLDER__, __SKILL_NAME_PLACEHOLDER__, and __SKILL_DESCRIPTION_PLACEHOLDER__, so opening it directly produces an unusable page. comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Root cause: placeholder substitution steps were stripped during SKILL.md rewrite

**What**: The installed skill (`.opencode/skills/skill-creator/SKILL.md`, lines 364-371) has the correct 5-step flow for using `assets/eval_review.html`:

1. Read the template from `assets/eval_review.html`
2. Replace the three placeholders (`__EVAL_DATA_PLACEHOLDER__`, `__SKILL_NAME_PLACEHOLDER__`, `__SKILL_DESCRIPTION_PLACEHOLDER__`)
3. Write the rendered result to a temp file and open it
4. User edits in browser, clicks Export
5. Agent reads the exported eval_set.json

The ported source (`ai-resources/skills/opencode-coder-skill-creator/SKILL.md`, lines 239-254) was rewritten by task opencode-coder-a1p.5 and collapsed this into:

> "2. Use `assets/eval_review.html` to let user edit and confirm the set."

No mention of reading the template, substituting placeholders, or writing a rendered output file. The critical render step (step 2 in the original) was completely dropped. This is a documentation regression introduced during the OpenCode port — the rewriter stripped the implementation detail while preserving only the intent.

**Why**: Without the substitution steps, an agent following the SKILL.md instructions will either: (a) open the raw template, which will crash on `const EVAL_DATA = __EVAL_DATA_PLACEHOLDER__;` (a JavaScript syntax error), or (b) tell the user to open it directly, resulting in a blank/broken page. The flow is 100% non-functional as documented.

**Suggested action**: Restore the explicit placeholder-substitution steps in the ported SKILL.md. See next comment for the specific fix recommendation.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Preferred fix: documentation-only — restore render steps with honest headless fallback

**What**: The fix should be documentation-only: rewrite SKILL.md lines 239-254 to restore the explicit template-render-write-open steps while adding an OpenCode-appropriate headless fallback. No new helper script is needed.

The replacement for the "Trigger Description Review" section should contain:

1. Draft 16-20 trigger queries (same as now)
2. Read the template from `assets/eval_review.html`
3. Replace placeholders:
   - `__EVAL_DATA_PLACEHOLDER__` → JSON array of eval items (no quotes — it is a JS variable assignment)
   - `__SKILL_NAME_PLACEHOLDER__` → skill name
   - `__SKILL_DESCRIPTION_PLACEHOLDER__` → current description
4. Write rendered HTML to a workspace temp file (e.g., `<workspace>/eval_review_<skill-name>.html`)
5. Attempt to open with platform-appropriate command (`open`, `xdg-open`, `start`)
6. If no GUI/browser is available, present the eval set as a JSON table in chat and let the user edit interactively — do not attempt to open files that will fail silently
7. Read the exported/confirmed eval set and proceed

This mirrors the installed skill's proven pattern (lines 364-371) while adding the headless fallback the ported version attempted to document.

**Why**: A helper script is overkill for string replacement that any agent can do inline. The installed skill already proves this flow works without a script — the agent reads the template, does three string replacements, writes a file, and opens it. Adding a Python script increases maintenance surface and introduces a dependency (Python must be available) for zero functional benefit. The SKILL.md is literally instructions to an AI agent — the agent IS the script.

**Suggested action**: Replace SKILL.md lines 239-254 with the steps above, modeled on the installed skill's lines 360-373 but adapted for OpenCode constraints.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Minimum acceptable fix: just add one sentence about placeholder substitution

**What**: If a full section rewrite is out of scope, the absolute minimum fix is adding one instruction between the current steps 1 and 2:

> "Read `assets/eval_review.html`, replace `__EVAL_DATA_PLACEHOLDER__` with the JSON array of eval items, `__SKILL_NAME_PLACEHOLDER__` with the skill name, and `__SKILL_DESCRIPTION_PLACEHOLDER__` with the current description. Write the result to a temp file before opening."

This makes the flow mechanically correct, even if it is less polished than the full rewrite.

**Why**: The current wording is not just suboptimal — it is broken. Any fix that makes the placeholder substitution explicit, even as a single sentence, moves the flow from "will produce a JavaScript error" to "will work." The bar for minimum acceptability is: an agent reading these instructions must know it cannot open the raw template.

**Suggested action**: Apply either this minimum fix or the full rewrite from the previous comment. The minimum fix is acceptable only if a follow-up is filed to align with the installed skill's more detailed pattern.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Why NOT a helper script: complexity vs. value analysis

**What**: The bug description suggests "add an OpenCode-safe helper that generates a usable review file" as one option. I recommend against this.

Evidence that a script is unnecessary:
1. The installed skill at `.opencode/skills/skill-creator/SKILL.md` already proves the agent-inline approach works — lines 364-369 tell the agent to do string replacement directly, no script involved.
2. The `eval-viewer/generate_review.py` exists as a helper for the MORE complex eval-viewer flow (which embeds run data, grading, benchmark results from multiple directories). The eval_review.html flow is three simple string replacements — fundamentally simpler.
3. A helper script would need: Python available, correct import paths, argument parsing, error handling. The agent doing `str.replace()` three times on a template has zero dependencies.
4. The skill already states "Do not assume browser availability" (line 38) — the headless fallback (present JSON in chat) must exist regardless of whether there is a script. The script would only handle the happy path.

The only scenario where a script would be justified: if this template were used by automated pipelines (not agents). But this section is explicitly "Manual path, automation tracked separately" (line 239).

**Why**: Adding a script to solve a documentation problem creates maintenance burden. When the template changes (new placeholders, different structure), both the script and the docs would need updating. With docs-only, only one thing needs to stay in sync.

**Suggested action**: Keep the fix documentation-only. If someone later wants a script for automation, that belongs in the separate automation task (opencode-coder-a1p.2), not in this bug fix.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Acceptance checks the implementation must satisfy

**What**: The fix for this bug, whether minimal or full, must pass these checks:

1. **Mechanical correctness**: An agent reading the fixed section must know to substitute all three placeholders before attempting to open or use the HTML file. Grep for `__EVAL_DATA_PLACEHOLDER__`, `__SKILL_NAME_PLACEHOLDER__`, and `__SKILL_DESCRIPTION_PLACEHOLDER__` — all three must be mentioned in the SKILL.md instructions.

2. **Write-before-open**: The instructions must explicitly say to write the rendered HTML to a new file (not modify the template in place). The template asset must remain a reusable template.

3. **Headless fallback is honest**: The fallback for no-GUI environments must be actionable — "review the JSON directly in chat" or "present the eval set as an editable table in conversation." It must NOT say "open the file" with a vague "if that fails..." — the fallback must be a first-class path.

4. **No new dependencies introduced**: The fix should not require Python, Node, or any tool beyond what the agent already has (file read, string manipulation, file write).

5. **Consistency with installed skill**: The ported instructions should produce the same functional outcome as the installed skill's lines 360-373, adapted for OpenCode's headless-first posture.

6. **Template asset unchanged**: `assets/eval_review.html` should NOT be modified as part of this fix. The placeholders are correct by design — the bug is in the instructions, not the template.

**Why**: These checks ensure the fix actually resolves the bug rather than creating a different broken state. Check 3 in particular matters because the original installed skill (line 371) assumes `~/Downloads` exists and the user can click "Export" in a browser — both assumptions the ported version correctly tried to address but failed by also dropping the render steps.

**Suggested action**: Use these as acceptance criteria when closing this bug. A verifier should be able to check all 6 in under 5 minutes.

title: Write design guide for OpenCode command authoring
description:
## Description
Capture the command-authoring design conclusions from this session in a reusable design note under `docs/design/`. The document should explain how to write OpenCode commands in general, how commands relate to skills, why reusable logic should usually live in skills instead of commands, and the style rules that keep command content concise and agent-relevant.

## Instructions
1. Create `docs/design/how-to-write-commands.md`.
2. Keep the guidance OpenCode-level and generic rather than project-specific.
3. Explain the command/skill split and the design rationale behind it, including why commands are treated as user entrypoints while skills hold reusable workflow logic.
4. Include guidance on argument handling, especially that meaningful user input should be wired intentionally.
5. Include style guidance for command writing, including avoiding "Use this when..." prose inside command bodies and keeping command content concise because tokens matter.
6. Make the document practical enough to guide future command authors.

## Files to Modify
- docs/design/how-to-write-commands.md — new design guidance for OpenCode command authoring

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A new `docs/design/how-to-write-commands.md` file exists
- [ ] The document explains the general OpenCode command model and its relation to skills without repo-specific coupling
- [ ] The document explains the rationale for keeping reusable logic in skills and commands as thin shortcuts
- [ ] The document includes explicit guidance on style, concision, and intentional argument handling
close_reason: Guide updated and verified

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text: Refined frontmatter guidance: agent, subtask, and model should be documented as rare overrides. Prefer letting the user select an agent explicitly when needed; hardcode agent only for true shortcut commands such as a dedicated security-review flow. Use subtask=true rarely, mainly for isolated operations such as commit workflows. Use model overrides rarely as well, for example on simple utility flows where a cheaper model is a deliberate tradeoff.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Guide violates its own concision advice — 358 lines is a long document

**What**: The guide is 358 lines and includes 3 worked examples, 2 duplicate explanations of the same layering model (sections "Core Model" and "Why We Write Commands This Way"), a full "Author Checklist" that restates what's already in the layering rules, and separate "Layering Rules" / "Style Rules" sections that overlap heavily. The guide tells authors "keep commands concise" and "tokens matter," but the guide itself is a long, repetitive document.

**Why**: A command author who reads this guide will get the message "be concise" surrounded by ~350 lines of repeated reasoning. That's ironic, and it weakens the credibility of the advice. If someone skims this, the signal-to-noise ratio is low. The guide should model the behavior it recommends.

**Suggested action**: Cut the guide to roughly half its current length. Merge "Core Model" and "Why We Write Commands This Way" into a single section. Merge "Layering Rules" and "Style Rules" into one section. Drop the Author Checklist (it just restates the rules). Collapse the three frontmatter examples into one annotated example that shows optional fields commented out. Target ~150-180 lines.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## "Layering Rules" section is structurally broken — only "Put this in the command" appears under it

**What**: Lines 62-68 define "Layering Rules" with a subsection "Put this in the command." But the companion subsections "Put this in the skill" (line 180) and "Put this in references" (line 189) appear ~120 lines later, after the entire Frontmatter Guidance and agent/subtask/model sections. They are orphaned from their parent heading — "Put this in the skill" and "Put this in references" appear to be siblings of "Default Recommendation" rather than children of "Layering Rules."

**Why**: A reader following the document structure will see "Layering Rules" → "Put this in the command" and then move on. The skill and references parts are buried far below and read like afterthoughts. The three-part layering model (command / skill / references) is the guide's central claim — burying 2/3 of it is a structural mistake.

**Suggested action**: Move "Put this in the skill" and "Put this in references" immediately after "Put this in the command" so all three are visually grouped as siblings under "Layering Rules." Then put the Frontmatter / agent/subtask/model content after the layering section.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Guide says nothing about what happens when a command loads a skill that loads references

**What**: The guide describes three layers (command → skill → references) but never explains the loading mechanics. When a command says "Load the X skill," does the agent literally call skill({ name: "X" })? Does the skill then auto-load its references, or must the command explicitly name them? The current commands show both patterns — some name specific references (docs.md names references/project-structure.md and references/project-docs-lifecycle.md), while others just say "load the skill." The guide does not address this.

**Why**: This is the most important practical question a command author faces, and the guide punts on it. Without clear guidance, authors will continue to sometimes list specific references in the command (duplicating routing logic that should live in the skill) and sometimes not. That inconsistency is exactly what the guide is supposed to prevent.

**Suggested action**: Add a short section explaining: (1) commands should load the skill, (2) the skill owns which references to use for which workflow, (3) commands should NOT enumerate references unless there is a specific reason to override the skill's default routing. State the expected calling convention explicitly.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Guide never defines what "thin" means concretely

**What**: The guide says commands should be "thin," "concise," "small by default," and a "shortcut" — but never gives a concrete threshold. Is 20 lines thin? 50? 100? The "Recommended Command Shape" example is ~15 lines. The "When a Command Can Be More Self-Contained" escape hatch says commands can be larger if they are "very small" and "utility-like" — which is circular.

**Why**: Without a concrete target, every author will have a different interpretation of "thin." The current init.md is 265 lines and doctor.md is 59 lines — both were presumably written by people who thought they were being concise. A rule that everyone interprets differently is not a rule.

**Suggested action**: State a concrete guideline, e.g.: "A typical thin command wrapper should be under 30 lines of body content (excluding frontmatter). Commands over 50 lines almost certainly contain logic that belongs in a skill. Commands over 100 lines are workflow documents, not commands." Pick numbers that match the intended architecture and state them.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Guide's treatment of the "Use /foo when..." anti-pattern is too weak

**What**: Line 205 says "Avoid patterns like: 'Use /foo when...'" — but this is buried in the Style Rules section as a single bullet. Meanwhile, every single current command (docs.md line 7, doctor.md line 7, dump-session.md line 7, improve-doc.md line 7, init.md line 7, status.md line 7) opens with exactly this pattern. The guide identifies the anti-pattern but does not explain why it wastes tokens or what to replace it with.

**Why**: This is the #1 most common violation in the current command set — a 100% violation rate. If the guide is going to call it an anti-pattern, it needs to be more prominent and more actionable. A single buried bullet will not change behavior.

**Suggested action**: Elevate this to a named anti-pattern with a before/after example. Show the current "Use /opencode-coder/docs when you want help..." pattern and the recommended replacement (just start with the instruction). Make it one of the first style rules, not the last.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Guide does not address H1 headings in command bodies

**What**: Every current command includes an H1 heading as the first line of body content (e.g., "# Project Docs Lifecycle", "# Coder Doctor", "# Export Session Data"). The guide never mentions whether this is expected, optional, or wasteful.

**Why**: An H1 heading in a command body is prose for a human reader — the agent already knows what command it is running. If the guide's position is "write for the invoked agent, not for a browser reader" (line 199), then these headings are token waste and should be called out. If they serve an OpenCode rendering purpose, that should be documented. Either way, the guide is silent on a pattern present in 100% of current commands.

**Suggested action**: Take a position. Either say "skip H1 headings in command bodies because the agent does not need them" or say "include a short H1 if OpenCode renders it in the UI." Do not leave it ambiguous.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Recommended Command Shape example does not match any current command

**What**: The recommended shape (lines 263-280) shows a clean pattern: frontmatter → "Load the skill" → "$ARGUMENTS" → "Follow the workflow" → "Return a report." Zero current commands match this pattern. The closest is report-bug.md, but even that includes extra sections (Requirements, numbered workflow steps, a blockquote). The recommended shape is aspirational but completely disconnected from reality.

**Why**: When the reference example and the real examples diverge completely, authors will follow the real examples — not the guide. The guide needs to either match current practice or explicitly flag that current commands need refactoring (which it does not do).

**Suggested action**: Since there is already an epic to refactor all commands (opencode-coder-al7), add a note in the guide that the recommended shape is the target and existing commands are being refactored to comply. Without that context, the guide reads like it describes a world that does not exist.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Guide's argument handling section is too abstract — no concrete frontmatter or wiring example

**What**: The Argument Handling section (lines 238-256) explains that commands should use $ARGUMENTS or $1/$2 placeholders, but never shows what this looks like in frontmatter or how OpenCode actually resolves these. The examples show command-line usage ("/review src/auth.ts") but not the command file content that wires those arguments. The recommended shape example later does show $ARGUMENTS in context, but the dedicated argument section itself lacks the concrete wiring.

**Why**: An author reading the argument section will understand "use $ARGUMENTS" conceptually but not know the exact syntax, whether it goes in the body or frontmatter, or how it interacts with skill loading. The guide buries the concrete usage in a different section (the recommended shape), so an author following the document linearly misses it.

**Suggested action**: Add a single concrete before/after in the argument section showing the command body with $ARGUMENTS wired in. Move or cross-reference the relevant part of the recommended shape example.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Guide mentions skill({ name: "X" }) calling convention zero times

**What**: The guide repeatedly says "load the skill" but never shows the actual calling convention. The current commands use two different patterns: some use a code block with skill({ name: "opencode-coder" }) (doctor.md, init.md), some use inline markdown "Load the opencode-coder skill" (docs.md, improve-doc.md, report-bug.md), and some do not load a skill at all (dump-session.md, status.md). The guide does not specify which pattern is correct.

**Why**: If the guide is the authority on how to write commands, it should specify how to invoke a skill. Otherwise different commands will use different conventions, making the codebase inconsistent and making it unclear whether the skill() call is required or just advisory.

**Suggested action**: Pick one canonical pattern and document it. If OpenCode resolves skill loading from a simple markdown instruction like "Load the X skill," say so. If it requires a tool call, say so. If both work identically, say that too.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text: Implemented the second-pass rewrite of docs/design/how-to-write-commands.md. Incorporated review feedback: shortened and reorganized the guide, clarified command → skill → reference layering, documented the canonical skill-loading pattern, added practical thinness thresholds, strengthened the ban on `Use /foo when...`, discouraged unnecessary H1 headings, added concrete `$ARGUMENTS` wiring, and kept the guidance generic to OpenCode.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text: Verification result: PASS. The guide now exists, stays generic to OpenCode, explains the command/skill/reference split and rationale, includes frontmatter guidance for description plus rare-use agent/subtask/model, includes style guidance and explicit argument wiring, defines thinness practically, and notes that existing commands may predate the target pattern.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Task .4 title is stale — still says "Define source-of-truth and sync path" but scope changed to aimgr swap

**What**: Task .4 was originally created to address the dual-copy problem (ai-resources/ vs .opencode/skills/). Its title is "Define source-of-truth and sync path for the vendored skill creator copy." But the user clarified that the solution is aimgr packaging — not sync-path definition. The description and instructions were updated to reflect aimgr, but the title still implies the old scope ("source-of-truth and sync path"). The comment on .4 confirms: "User decided the source-of-truth path will be handled via aimgr packaging."

**Why**: A stale title misleads anyone scanning the backlog. The actual task is "Switch to aimgr-packaged skill-creator and remove Anthropic entry" — which is narrower and clearer than "define source-of-truth and sync path."

**Suggested action**: Rename to "Switch project to aimgr-packaged opencode-coder-skill-creator" or "Replace Anthropic skill-creator with aimgr-packaged OpenCode version."

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Task .4 should execute early, not late — it unblocks live testing

**What**: Task .4 (aimgr packaging swap) has no explicit dependency on .1, .2, or .5. Its current priority is 2 (lower than the others at priority 1). But logically, .4 should execute BEFORE the implementation tasks, or at least early enough that the smoke test (if added) can use the aimgr-installed skill. The aimgr swap ensures the live installed skill at .opencode/skills/ points to the new opencode-coder-skill-creator content. Without this, implementation tasks modify ai-resources/ files that are not the live copy OpenCode loads.

**Why**: If .4 runs last, all the implementation work (.1, .2, .5) modifies files under ai-resources/skills/opencode-coder-skill-creator/ that OpenCode is not actually loading. The live copy at .opencode/skills/skill-creator/ remains unchanged until aimgr syncs. This means nobody can test the ported skill during development — they would need to manually copy files or run aimgr install between each implementation task. By doing .4 first or early, we establish the pipeline so that changes flow to the live path automatically.

**Suggested action**: Raise .4 to priority 1. Remove its dependency on other implementation tasks (it can run independently). Consider making .4 block the implementation tasks (.1, .5, .2) so the aimgr pipeline is set up before content changes begin. At minimum, .4 must block any smoke test task.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## The .opencode/skills/skill-creator/ copy is identical to ai-resources/ — dual-copy problem is confirmed but simpler than originally thought

**What**: I verified that .opencode/skills/skill-creator/SKILL.md has identical content to ai-resources/skills/opencode-coder-skill-creator/SKILL.md (same frontmatter, same body). The prior comment (019d1c3a-a03b) flagged the dual-copy risk. With a1p.4 now resolving this via aimgr, the problem has a clear solution — but there is a timing issue: if implementation tasks (.1, .2, .5) modify files under ai-resources/ before a1p.4 sets up the aimgr pipeline, the .opencode/skills/skill-creator/ copy will be stale during development.

Also notable: the installed skill directory is named "skill-creator" (the original Anthropic name) while the ai-resources copy is named "opencode-coder-skill-creator" (the new name). After aimgr swap, the installed directory name will presumably change. Task .4 should verify what the installed directory name becomes after aimgr install and whether it affects skill triggering (the SKILL.md frontmatter name field is "opencode-coder-skill-creator").

**Why**: If the installed directory name changes from "skill-creator" to "opencode-coder-skill-creator", any existing references to the old name will break. This needs to be verified during a1p.4, not discovered during acceptance review.

**Suggested action**: Add to a1p.4's acceptance criteria: "The installed skill directory name and SKILL.md frontmatter name are consistent and the skill triggers correctly under the new name." Also add a1p.4 instruction to verify no other files reference the old "skill-creator" skill name.

title: Manual launcher shell mode triggers zsh first-run prompt in isolated HOME
description:
## Description
When the manual launcher runs in shell mode and inherits SHELL=/bin/zsh, the isolated HOME used by the launcher has no zsh startup files, so zsh opens with the interactive zsh-newuser-install screen instead of a clean shell prompt.

## Reproduction
1. In this repo, run:
   SHELL=/bin/zsh bun run test:manual -- --mode=shell --fixture=cli-smoke-project
2. Observe the shell session after launcher setup.

## Expected
Shell mode should open directly into the requested isolated shell session without unexpected first-run setup UI.

## Actual
zsh shows the zsh-newuser-install wizard before the shell prompt. This adds unexpected interaction and can interfere with the intended manual-launcher shell UX.

## Evidence
Observed during acceptance review of opencode-coder-g3l on 2026-03-23. The launcher printed the normal setup summary, then zsh displayed the first-run configuration screen because HOME was isolated.
close_reason: Fixed manual launcher shell mode to seed isolated zsh startup file and prevent zsh-newuser-install prompt under isolated HOME.

title: Ignore and clean up e2e failure artifacts
description:
## Description
The e2e harness writes failure diagnostics under `tests/e2e/.artifacts/`, but that directory is currently not gitignored and some generated artifact files are already tracked in git. We need a sane, test-maintainer-friendly policy for where these artifacts live, how they are inspected, and how stale copies are cleaned up.

The current location is probably reasonable because it is test-local and already documented, but the workflow is incomplete unless generated artifacts are ignored, currently tracked artifact files are removed from the index, and there is a repeatable cleanup path.

Verification review concluded that the overall plan is sound, but it needs explicit handling for tracked-file migration and stale per-scenario data.

## Instructions
1. Keep `tests/e2e/.artifacts/` as the diagnostics location unless implementation work reveals a concrete reason it should move.
2. Add git ignore coverage for generated e2e artifacts so new failure logs do not show up as untracked files.
3. Remove any currently tracked files under `tests/e2e/.artifacts/` from the git index while preserving the intended local/generated workflow.
4. Add an explicit cleanup path for e2e artifacts.
   - Prefer a package script such as `clean:e2e-artifacts`.
   - Do not automatically delete all historical failure evidence on every default `test:e2e` run unless there is a strong reason; if you want a fresh-run mode, prefer making it explicit.
5. Review the harness write path and ensure repeated failures for the same scenario cannot leave stale extra files in that scenario folder.
6. Update testing documentation so contributors know:
   - what the directory is for
   - that it is intentionally untracked
   - how to clear it
   - whether artifacts persist across runs until manually cleaned
7. Verify the chosen workflow works in practice by exercising both artifact generation and cleanup.

## Files to Modify
- `.gitignore` — ignore `tests/e2e/.artifacts/`
- `package.json` — add cleanup script and optional fresh-run entrypoint only if justified
- `tests/e2e/helpers/harness.ts` — clean stale per-scenario artifacts if needed
- `docs/TESTING.md` — document artifact purpose, retention, and cleanup workflow
- tracked files under `tests/e2e/.artifacts/` — remove from version control if they are generated outputs

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] New generated files under `tests/e2e/.artifacts/` are ignored by git
- [ ] Previously tracked generated artifact files under `tests/e2e/.artifacts/` are removed from the git index
- [ ] There is a documented, repeatable cleanup path for e2e artifacts
- [ ] Re-running the same scenario cannot leave stale extra files in that scenario folder
- [ ] Contributors can tell from `docs/TESTING.md` what the folder is for, whether it persists, and how to clear it
- [ ] Practical verification proves the workflow works:
  - generate an artifact and confirm it is ignored by git
  - confirm `git status --short -- tests/e2e/.artifacts` is clean for generated files
  - exercise the cleanup command and confirm artifacts are removed
close_reason: Implemented and verified e2e artifact workflow: artifacts ignored, previously tracked files removed from index, clean:e2e-artifacts works, and per-scenario rewrite clears stale files.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## This is a duplicate of opencode-coder-mx1 — same root cause, same fix

**What**: 53y reports scenario 3 failing with command list `["init", "review", "opencode-coder/init"]` and expected docs lifecycle commands missing. This is the identical symptom, root cause, and code path as opencode-coder-mx1 (scenario 1). The root cause is that aimgr is not on PATH in the e2e environment. When aimgr is absent, `AimgrService.isAimgrAvailable()` returns false, `verifyResources()` returns null, `verifyAndAutoRepairResources()` returns `resourcesHealthy: false`, and the gating in `src/index.ts:273-274` correctly suppresses docs lifecycle commands. The test then fails because it unconditionally asserts those commands should be present.

The only difference between scenarios 1 and 3 is that scenario 3 runs `opencode run --command pwd` first, then probes via real-server. But the real-server probe is a fresh server start that goes through the same startup flow. Without aimgr, the outcome is identical.

**Why**: Fixing mx1 will fix 53y. There is zero independent work to do here. Keeping this open alongside mx1 creates confusion about how many problems exist (answer: one).

**Suggested action**: Close as duplicate of opencode-coder-mx1. All review findings and root cause analysis have been posted on mx1.

title: E2E scenarios 1 and 3 unconditionally assert docs lifecycle commands but require aimgr on PATH
description:
## Description
E2E scenarios 1 and 3 currently call docs-lifecycle command assertions unconditionally. That expectation only holds when `aimgr` is available on `PATH` and resource verification can mark the project healthy.

In aimgr-absent environments, the product behavior is currently correct: runtime resource verification reports unhealthy/unavailable state, docs lifecycle commands stay suppressed, and the real defect is that the tests still expect those commands to be present.

## Root Cause
- `AimgrService.isAimgrAvailable()` returns false when `aimgr` is not installed or not on `PATH`
- resource verification cannot mark the project healthy
- `projectContext.aimgr.resourcesHealthy` stays false
- runtime correctly exposes only the non-docs command surface
- scenarios 1 and 3 still assert docs lifecycle commands unconditionally

## Instructions
1. Update e2e coverage so scenarios 1 and 3 explicitly account for aimgr availability instead of always expecting docs lifecycle commands.
2. Preserve validation of active startup and plugin load even when aimgr is unavailable.
3. When aimgr is available, continue asserting docs lifecycle command exposure.
4. Update contributor/testing docs only if the conditional prerequisite needs to be called out explicitly.
5. Re-run targeted integration and e2e coverage for the affected scenarios.

## Files to Modify
- `tests/e2e/opencode.test.ts` — make scenario 1 and 3 command assertions conditional on aimgr availability
- `tests/e2e/helpers/harness.ts` — add or expose an aimgr availability helper if needed
- `docs/TESTING.md` — document the aimgr prerequisite if command expectations become conditional

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Scenario 1 passes whether aimgr is present or absent
- [ ] Scenario 3 passes whether aimgr is present or absent
- [ ] Tests still assert docs lifecycle command exposure when aimgr is available
- [ ] Tests still verify active startup/plugin load when aimgr is unavailable
- [ ] Documentation matches the implemented prerequisite behavior
close_reason: E2E assertions now match aimgr-gated runtime behavior; targeted e2e and integration coverage pass.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## These two bugs (mx1 and 53y) are the same defect, not two separate bugs

**What**: Both mx1 and 53y report the identical symptom: command list is `["init", "review", "opencode-coder/init"]` with docs lifecycle commands missing. Both occur in e2e scenarios (1 and 3 respectively). Both were discovered at the same time from the same verification session. The reported command list is byte-for-byte identical. The actual/expected behavior descriptions are functionally identical. The only difference is scenario 1 uses `getPluginSignalsViaRealServer` directly while scenario 3 uses `runOpencodeCli` followed by `getPluginSignalsViaRealServer`. But the failure occurs in the same code path: the real-server probe's `command.list` call, which reflects what `config()` registered.

**Why**: Two separate bugs for the same defect fragments the fix. A tasker would need to investigate mx1, determine the root cause, fix it, then open 53y and discover it's the same root cause with the same fix. This wastes a session. Worse, if different assignees take them, they'll duplicate analysis and potentially produce conflicting fixes.

**Suggested action**: Merge into a single bug. Close 53y as a duplicate of mx1, or close mx1 as a duplicate of 53y, or close both and create one replacement bug. The surviving issue should reference both scenarios. Recommendation: keep mx1 (it's the more direct test — scenario 1 has fewer moving parts) and close 53y as duplicate.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Root cause identified: aimgr not on PATH in e2e environment, not a command registration bug

**What**: I reproduced both scenario 1 and scenario 3. Both fail with the same symptom: `["init", "review", "opencode-coder/init"]`. The root cause is that `aimgr` is not installed on this machine (`which aimgr` returns nothing). The gating logic in `src/index.ts:273-274` is:

```typescript
const docsLifecycleResourcesAvailable =
  activeMode !== null && projectContext?.aimgr.resourcesHealthy === true;
```

When `aimgr` is not on PATH, `AimgrService.verifyResources()` calls `isAimgrAvailable()` which returns false, so `verifyResources()` returns null. `verifyAndAutoRepairResources()` then returns `resourcesHealthy: false`. The `projectDetector.detectAndWrite()` receives `resourcesHealthyOverride: false` and writes `aimgr.resourcesHealthy: false` into project.yaml. The gating correctly suppresses docs commands.

The earlier bug opencode-coder-3fr was closed with a fix that added `ai.package.yaml` with `resources: []` to the existing-active-project fixture. That fix was CORRECT for environments where aimgr IS installed — the verify call would see no issues and return healthy. But it does NOTHING when aimgr is not on PATH, because the verify flow never reads ai.package.yaml — it short-circuits at `isAimgrAvailable()`.

**Why**: This bug is not "docs lifecycle commands are missing from e2e scenarios." This bug is "e2e scenarios 1 and 3 require aimgr to be installed, which is an undocumented environment prerequisite for those e2e assertions." The product code is working exactly as designed. The test expectations are wrong for aimgr-absent environments.

**Suggested action**: The fix is one of:
1. **Make tests conditional**: Skip `expectDocsLifecycleCommands()` assertions when aimgr is not on PATH. The test should still verify the server starts, the coder tool loads, and init is registered. But docs lifecycle command assertions should be gated on aimgr availability.
2. **Mock aimgr in the fixture**: Create a stub `aimgr` script in the test PATH that returns `{"status": "ok", "issues": []}` for `aimgr verify --format json`. This is more complex but makes the test deterministic everywhere.
3. **Document the prerequisite**: Add aimgr to the required environment for full e2e pass and mark these assertions as skip-if-unavailable.

Recommendation: option 1 is simplest and most honest. The tests already have skip-if patterns (e.g., `resolveCopilotAuthSeedFromEnv()` for scenario 5). Apply the same pattern for aimgr availability.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## This bug is a duplicate of opencode-coder-3fr, not an independent defect

**What**: opencode-coder-3fr was filed, diagnosed, and "closed" for exactly this symptom: "E2E real-server existing active project omits docs lifecycle commands." The 3fr close reason says the fix was "added committed ai.package.yaml (resources: []) so first real-server startup reports resources healthy and docs lifecycle commands register deterministically; scenario 1 now passes." But scenario 1 does NOT pass on machines without aimgr installed. The 3fr fix was incomplete — it addressed one sub-cause (missing ai.package.yaml) but not the actual blocker (aimgr binary absent from PATH).

opencode-coder-mx1 is rediscovering the same defect that 3fr was supposed to fix. It is not a new or different bug.

**Why**: If this is treated as a new standalone bug, the history of investigation in 3fr (which contains excellent root cause analysis in its comments) will be missed. The tasker will repeat the same investigation. The fix for mx1 should be informed by the 3fr analysis — specifically the comment (019d1694-3afa) which correctly identified the fixture/environment gap.

**Suggested action**: Either:
- Reopen 3fr and close mx1 as duplicate, then fix 3fr properly (handle aimgr-absent environments)
- Or keep mx1 but add an explicit dependency/link to 3fr and include the 3fr analysis context in the description so the tasker doesn't start from scratch

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Description is misleading: says "omits docs lifecycle commands" but the product behavior is correct

**What**: The bug title says "Real-server active startup path omits docs lifecycle commands in scenario 1." This frames it as a product defect in command registration. But the product code is working correctly — when aimgr resources cannot be verified as healthy, docs lifecycle commands SHOULD be suppressed (this is the gating logic from opencode-coder-67d). The actual problem is that the e2e test asserts docs lifecycle commands are present without ensuring the prerequisites for those commands are met.

The description says "expected docs lifecycle commands are missing" but does not distinguish between:
- (a) the product failing to register commands it should register
- (b) the test expecting commands that cannot be registered in this environment

It is case (b).

**Why**: A tasker reading this bug would look at the command registration code in `src/index.ts` for a defect. There is no defect there. They would waste time investigating healthy product code. The bug should direct attention to the test expectations and environment prerequisites.

**Suggested action**: Rewrite the title and description to reflect the actual problem:
- Title: "E2E scenarios 1 and 3 unconditionally assert docs lifecycle commands but require aimgr on PATH"
- Type: This is a test defect, not a product bug. Consider type=task instead of type=bug.
- Description should include the root cause (aimgr not on PATH → verify returns null → resources unhealthy → commands correctly suppressed) and point to the fix area (test assertions, not product code).

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Should this be linked under epic opencode-coder-lg2?

**What**: These bugs were discovered during f6l.5 verification, but the underlying feature (docs lifecycle commands, resource gating) was implemented as part of epic opencode-coder-lg2. The existing bug opencode-coder-3fr was already tracked under lg2.6 and was closed as part of that epic's acceptance work. mx1 is effectively a reopening of 3fr (the same scenario 1 failure) that the 3fr fix did not fully address.

**Why**: If mx1 stays as a standalone bug with only a `discovered-from: f6l.5` dependency, it loses the context of the lg2 epic where all the related investigation, fixes, and acceptance criteria live. The acceptance task lg2.6 is still in_progress. The epic comment (019d17a7-dd02) says "acceptance review complete: epic is ready to close pending 2 housekeeping actions" — but scenario 1 is clearly NOT passing, which means lg2.6 acceptance criterion "automated command-registration coverage exists" is not met.

**Suggested action**: 
1. Link mx1 to lg2.6 (blocks relationship) — this bug is a direct blocker for the lg2 acceptance task
2. Or better: reopen 3fr with the aimgr-absent root cause, close mx1/53y as duplicates, and complete the 3fr fix properly
3. Either way, do NOT close the lg2 epic until this is resolved — the "ready to close" assessment was premature

title: Diagnostics bundle README reports readme artifact as missing
description:
## Description
While verifying `opencode-coder-yss.2`, the diagnostics collector produced valid bundles and `manifest.json` marked the `readme` artifact as `included`, but the generated `README.md` artifact table still reported `readme` as `missing`.

## Why This Matters
The bundle is intended to be self-describing for humans and agents. A contradictory artifact summary inside the bundle can mislead triage and reduces confidence in the exported evidence.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run `bun run diagnostics:collect` against any project root.
2. Open the generated `README.md` and inspect the `readme` row in the collected artifacts table.
3. Compare it with `manifest.json` for the same bundle.

## Actual Behavior
- `manifest.json` reports `artifacts.readme.status = "included"`.
- `README.md` shows the `readme` row as `missing`.

## Expected Behavior
- `README.md` should report the `readme` artifact as `included`.
- The README artifact table should stay consistent with `manifest.json`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Generated `README.md` reports the `readme` artifact as `included`
- [ ] `README.md` and `manifest.json` agree on artifact status for `readme`
- [ ] Deterministic coverage catches this regression
close_reason: Resolved diagnostics README/manifest inconsistency for readme artifact by updating write order and adding deterministic regression test.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text: Fixed root cause in diagnostics collector: README was generated before manifest.artifacts.readme status was updated to included. Updated flow to set readme artifact status first, then render README so the artifact table reflects included. Added deterministic unit test asserting README readme row is included and matches manifest status. Verified with bun test tests/unit/collect-diagnostics.test.ts and bun run typecheck.

title: Failing test: installed-configured manual launcher proof scenario times out
description:
Discovered while verifying opencode-coder-lg2.6.

## What was tested
1. Ran `bun test tests/e2e/manual-launcher.test.ts`.
2. Re-ran the failing case directly with `bun test tests/e2e/manual-launcher.test.ts --test-name-pattern "supports installed-configured plugin source with deterministic package prep and version proof"`.

## What was observed
- `tests/e2e/manual-launcher.test.ts` failed because `manual launcher non-interactive mode > supports installed-configured plugin source with deterministic package prep and version proof` timed out after 120000ms.
- The full suite reported 14 pass, 1 fail, 1 error.
- The isolated rerun also timed out after 120000ms.

## Why this matters
This is an actual failing automated verification in the repository during final acceptance review. Even if unrelated to the docs-lifecycle acceptance target, it must be tracked instead of being silently ignored.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `bun test tests/e2e/manual-launcher.test.ts` passes cleanly
- [ ] The installed-configured manual launcher proof scenario completes within its timeout budget
- [ ] The scenario still validates expected installed package/version proof behavior after the fix
close_reason: Replaced the installed-configured proof scenario's LLM-dependent path with deterministic installed-plugin initialization/version proof via the manual-launcher proof helper; tests/integration/manual-launcher.test.ts now passes cleanly within timeout.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Verdict: real test bug, not a flake — the test design requires a working LLM backend

**What**: The failing test at line 383 (`supports installed-configured plugin source with deterministic package prep and version proof`) runs `opencode run --command pwd --format json` as its child command. This invocation requires a working LLM backend connection. The opencode process starts, loads the plugin (which writes `pluginVersion: 0.34.2` to `.coder/project.yaml`), then hangs indefinitely waiting for the LLM to process the `/pwd` command execution. The 120s test timeout fires, bun kills the dangling opencode process, and the test fails.

I reproduced this deterministically — the setup phase completes successfully (auth seeded, plugin resolved, version wired), but `opencode run --command pwd --format json` produces no stdout and never exits.

**Why**: This is a **deterministic test design bug**, not infrastructure instability or a flake. The test tries to prove installed-configured plugin loading works, but it chose an LLM-dependent opencode invocation as the trigger. This will fail on any machine where the LLM call doesn't complete within 120s (stale auth tokens, network issues, rate limiting, or simply an LLM that takes too long for `/pwd`).

Compare with the test at line 220 (`runs one-shot command with shared isolated setup`) which uses `-- env` (not opencode at all) and passes reliably. And the negative test at line 454 which also uses `-- env` and passes.

**Suggested action**: Replace `opencode run --command pwd --format json` with a simpler opencode invocation that triggers plugin load and project.yaml write WITHOUT requiring LLM interaction. Candidates:
1. A non-LLM opencode command (e.g., `opencode debug` subcommand if it triggers plugin load)
2. Just starting and immediately exiting opencode (if that's enough to trigger plugin load + project.yaml write)
3. Keep `opencode run` but with a trivial prompt that has a very short timeout, or mock the LLM
4. Skip opencode entirely and use `env` like the other tests, then check project.yaml was written by the plugin load during startup

The proof mechanism already works — the launcher reads project.yaml after exit. The problem is that the vehicle for triggering plugin load (`opencode run --command pwd`) is overkill and environment-dependent.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## 6 duplicate open issues all describing the same timeout — consolidate into this one

**What**: There are 6 open issues (including this one) all describing the same symptom: the manual-launcher installed-configured e2e test times out after 120s:
- `opencode-coder-6yl` (this bug)
- `opencode-coder-2dt` — "Found: manual-launcher installed-configured e2e test times out"
- `opencode-coder-b8p` — "Found: manual-launcher installed-configured test exits 143/times out"
- `opencode-coder-0x0` — "Found: manual-launcher installed-configured e2e test times out intermittently"
- `opencode-coder-k3o` — "Found: manual-launcher installed-configured regression test times out"
- `opencode-coder-qfk` — "Found: manual-launcher installed-configured test times out and exits 143"

These were all created by different agents during different work sessions as "discovered work", each faithfully filing a new bug for the same symptom. They are all the same root cause (test uses LLM-dependent command as plugin-load trigger).

**Why**: 6 open bugs for 1 problem creates tracking noise and wastes triage time. The "intermittently" description in 0x0 is also misleading — this is deterministic, not intermittent.

**Suggested action**: Close 2dt, b8p, 0x0, k3o, and qfk as duplicates of this issue (6yl). This bug has the clearest title and is the one you asked me to review.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## This bug does NOT block lg2.6 acceptance — it is unrelated to the docs lifecycle scope

**What**: Bug 6yl is about the installed-configured plugin source e2e test timing out. The lg2.6 acceptance review is about verifying the published docs lifecycle commands and resources. The test at line 383 of manual-launcher.test.ts tests the manual launcher's installed-configured plugin loading proof mechanism. This is test infrastructure for comparing installed vs local-build plugins — it has nothing to do with docs lifecycle commands, slash commands, or any lg2 acceptance criteria.

The lg2.6 acceptance criteria are:
- Published project-setup guidance exists
- Init can guide doc setup
- One primary docs lifecycle command exists
- One incident-driven improve-doc command exists
- AGENTS-only maintenance superseded
- Team/stealth/incident functional scenarios
- Automated command-registration coverage

None of these require or depend on the installed-configured manual launcher proof test.

**Why**: If 6yl is treated as a blocker for lg2.6, the docs lifecycle acceptance review is held up by an unrelated test infrastructure bug. The two problems have completely different fix directions and should be tracked independently.

**Suggested action**: 
1. Remove any blocking relationship between 6yl and lg2.6
2. Track 6yl independently as a test-infrastructure bug (it already is via discovered-from:lg2.6)
3. Do not let 6yl delay lg2.6 acceptance review closure

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Bug is directly executable but the description needs sharpening

**What**: The current description says "installed-configured manual launcher proof scenario times out after 120000ms" but doesn't identify the root cause. The root cause is: the test uses `opencode run --command pwd --format json` which requires a working LLM backend, and this LLM call either hangs or exceeds 120s. The acceptance criteria are correct ("test passes cleanly" and "completes within timeout budget") but the description doesn't tell the executor what's actually wrong or what direction to fix.

**Why**: A tasker picking up this bug would waste time diagnosing the timeout instead of fixing it. The diagnosis is complete — the fix direction is clear. The description should reflect that.

**Suggested action**: Rewrite the description to include the precise problem statement:

**Precise problem**: The installed-configured proof test (line 383 of `tests/e2e/manual-launcher.test.ts`) uses `opencode run --command pwd --format json` as the vehicle to trigger plugin load. This command requires a working LLM backend. The opencode process starts, loads the plugin, writes `project.yaml` with the correct version, then hangs waiting for LLM response to the `/pwd` command. The 120s timeout fires.

**Minimal correct fix**: Replace `opencode run --command pwd --format json` with an opencode invocation that triggers plugin load and `project.yaml` write without requiring LLM interaction. The simplest approach is to use `opencode run "Respond with exactly: PROOF_OK" --format default` with a short inner timeout, or find a non-LLM opencode subcommand that still triggers plugin initialization. Alternatively, restructure to use `env` (like other tests) plus a separate check that `project.yaml` was written during plugin startup.

comments.text: Reviewer conclusion: real deterministic test-design bug. The installed-configured proof test uses an LLM-dependent `opencode run --command pwd --format json` invocation to trigger plugin load, so the process hangs waiting on the LLM even though plugin initialization already succeeded. Fix by switching the test to a non-LLM proof path that still verifies plugin initialization/version proof.
