title: Project-path launcher copies local .opencode and inherits broken symlink noise
description:
## Description
Discovered while verifying `opencode-coder-lg2.6`.

## Precise problem
This is primarily a **harness copy-scope bug**, not a repository-validity bug.

The manual launcher `--project-path` mode currently copies the source repository's local `.opencode/` directory into the isolated workspace. In this repository, `.opencode/` is local-only and may contain symlinks to external development resources. If those links are stale, the copied workspace inherits broken symlinks and OpenCode emits `failed to load command` ENOENT noise during startup.

## Root cause
`tests/e2e/helpers/harness.ts` excludes:
- `.git`
- `.beads`
- `.coder`

but it does **not** exclude `.opencode`.

That means isolated project-path runs inherit local developer-only `.opencode/commands` state even though the harness already rewires `.opencode/plugins/` intentionally for the plugin under test.

## Why this matters
This pollutes manual acceptance evidence with unrelated startup errors and makes the isolated workspace depend on local developer state.

## Correct scope
The right fix is to treat `.opencode/` like other local runtime/dev-only state for project-path copies.
This is about making the harness copy deterministic.

A follow-up repository-validation test is reasonable if we want to assert the tracked repo itself contains no broken committed links, but that is separate from this harness bug.

## Recommended fix direction
- exclude `.opencode/` from project-path copies in the harness
- add regression coverage that project-path copies do not inherit `.opencode/commands` noise
- optionally create a separate follow-up if we want a repo-validity check for committed resources

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Manual launcher project-path copies do not include source `.opencode/` runtime/dev-local state
- [ ] Startup no longer emits `failed to load command` ENOENT noise from copied broken `.opencode` links
- [ ] Regression coverage proves `.opencode` is excluded from project-path copies
close_reason: Excluded .opencode from project-path workspace copies in harness and added regression assertions in manual-launcher test to verify copied workspaces do not inherit .opencode command files/symlinks.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Bug misidentifies the root cause — this is a harness copy-scope problem, not a repo-contents problem

**What**: The `.opencode/` directory is gitignored (`.gitignore` line 21: `.opencode/`). Nothing in `.opencode/commands/` is tracked in git. The symlinks there are local dev-environment wiring created by `aimgr` (symlinks from `.opencode/commands/` → `~/dev/env/ai-repo/commands/` → `ai-resources/commands/` in this repo). The canonical, committed source of truth for commands is `ai-resources/commands/` which IS tracked in git and contains real files.

**Why**: This means the bug title "Repo-local .opencode command symlinks point to missing ai-repo files" is misleading. There are no repo-tracked broken symlinks. The problem is that the manual launcher's `--project-path` copy includes `.opencode/` (it's not in `EXCLUDED_COPY_SEGMENTS` at `harness.ts:100`), so local-only dev wiring leaks into isolated workspaces. When symlink targets happen to be missing (as `init.md` root-level and `update-agent-md.md` were at discovery time), the copied workspace inherits broken symlinks.

**Suggested action**: Reframe the bug as a harness copy-scope deficiency, not a repository content problem. The repo contents are fine — this is `.gitignore`d local dev state bleeding into test isolation.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## The two specific broken files from the bug are already gone

**What**: The bug cites two broken symlinks: `.opencode/commands/init.md` (root-level) and `.opencode/commands/opencode-coder/update-agent-md.md`. Neither of these symlinks currently exists in `.opencode/commands/`. The remaining 12 symlinks all resolve successfully through the `ai-repo` → `ai-resources/` chain.

**Why**: This means the original trigger has self-resolved (likely the local `ai-repo` wiring was updated). However, the underlying fragility remains — any future stale symlink in `.opencode/commands/` will reproduce this bug.

**Suggested action**: Don't close this as "already fixed." The structural vulnerability (harness copies untracked `.opencode/` directory including external symlinks) is still present.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## The correct fix is to add .opencode to EXCLUDED_COPY_SEGMENTS in the harness

**What**: `tests/e2e/helpers/harness.ts` line 100 defines `EXCLUDED_COPY_SEGMENTS = [".git", ".beads", ".coder"]`. The `.opencode` directory is missing from this list. The harness already re-creates `.opencode/plugins/` for plugin wiring in `wireBuiltPluginArtifact()`, so copying the source project's `.opencode/` is not only unnecessary — it actively introduces noise (stale symlinks, leftover node_modules, etc.).

**Why**: Adding `.opencode` to the exclusion list:
1. Prevents broken symlinks from leaking into isolated workspaces
2. Prevents local-dev command/skill/agent wiring from interfering with test isolation
3. Aligns with the existing pattern (`.git`, `.beads`, `.coder` are already excluded for the same "local state, not project content" reason)
4. The harness already rebuilds `.opencode/plugins/` from scratch, so there is no loss of test capability

**Suggested action**: The fix is a one-line change — add `".opencode"` to `EXCLUDED_COPY_SEGMENTS` at `harness.ts:100`:

```typescript
const EXCLUDED_COPY_SEGMENTS = [".git", ".beads", ".coder", ".opencode"] as const;
```

Files involved: `tests/e2e/helpers/harness.ts` (line 100).

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## A regression test should be added at the unit level for shouldCopyPath

**What**: `tests/e2e/manual-launcher.test.ts` exists for testing launcher behavior. A test should verify that `shouldCopyPath()` rejects `.opencode` paths. This is a unit-level assertion, not an e2e test.

**Why**: This is a correctness invariant on the harness itself. If someone changes the exclusion list, the test catches it immediately. The test is cheap (no CLI startup, no plugin build, no auth) and deterministic.

**Suggested action**: Add test cases asserting:
1. `shouldCopyPath(root, join(root, ".opencode"))` returns `false`
2. `shouldCopyPath(root, join(root, ".opencode", "commands", "init.md"))` returns `false`
3. Optionally, a small integration test using `createProjectPathWorkspace` on a temp source dir with a `.opencode/commands/broken-link.md` symlink, verifying it's absent in the copy.

Test level: unit (for `shouldCopyPath`). Note: `shouldCopyPath` is currently a module-private function — it may need to be exported or tested indirectly through `createProjectPathWorkspace`.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Bug label area:docs is wrong — this is area:testing

**What**: The bug is labeled `area:docs` but the problem and fix are entirely in the test harness (`tests/e2e/helpers/harness.ts`). No documentation files are involved.

**Why**: Incorrect labeling will route this to the wrong reviewers and misrepresent its scope.

**Suggested action**: Remove `area:docs`, add `area:testing`.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Acceptance criteria need rewriting — current criteria describe symptoms, not the fix

**What**: The current acceptance criteria are:
1. "Repo-local .opencode/commands no longer contains broken symlinks" — describes local dev state, not something this bug should fix
2. "Manual launcher project-path runs do not emit startup errors" — correct but vague
3. "Local-only command wiring is deterministic or excluded" — correct intent

**Why**: Criteria #1 conflates the local dev environment with the repository. The fix is in the harness, not in cleaning up symlinks. Criteria need to be testable against the harness change.

**Suggested action**: Replace acceptance criteria with:
- EXCLUDED_COPY_SEGMENTS in tests/e2e/helpers/harness.ts includes .opencode
- --project-path workspace copies do not contain .opencode/ from the source project
- A regression test verifies .opencode exclusion from project-path copies
- Manual launcher --project-path runs against this repo produce no "failed to load command" ENOENT errors for copied symlink artifacts

title: Shared isolated OpenCode config references missing @hk9890/opencode-dynatrace plugin
description: Discovered while verifying opencode-coder-lg2.6. Manual isolated runs that use the default seeded config from tests/e2e/fixtures/_shared/opencode-config/opencode.json log a startup error because the config still enables @hk9890/opencode-dynatrace@0.6.0, but OpenCode tries to install it from npm and gets 404. Evidence: manual docs-command run preserved log /tmp/opencode-coder-existing-active-project-t3EAbG/isolated-opencode/xdg-data/opencode/log/2026-03-22T174056.log shows service=plugin pkg=@hk9890/opencode-dynatrace version=0.6.0, then "error: GET https://registry.npmjs.org/@hk9890%2fopencode-dynatrace - 404 failed to install plugin" and session.error publishing. This means the documented shared manual/e2e baseline is not clean in this environment and injects unrelated startup errors into acceptance-style manual verification. Expected behavior: the shared isolated config should either avoid enabling unavailable external plugins in this test baseline, or provide a deterministic install path that does not emit session-startup errors during verification runs.
close_reason: Updated shared isolated opencode config to use empty plugin array, aligned manual-launcher assertions with empty shared plugin baseline, and updated e2e testing docs/fixture README to reflect no external plugin in shared config.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Verdict: This is a real config bug, but severity is lower than it appears

**What**: The bug is real. The shared config at `tests/e2e/fixtures/_shared/opencode-config/opencode.json` includes `@hk9890/opencode-dynatrace@0.6.0` in the `plugin` array. When OpenCode starts in isolated mode, it reads this config and tries to install that package from the public registry, gets a 404, and logs a startup error.

**Why this matters less than it seems**: The harness sets `OPENCODE_DISABLE_DEFAULT_PLUGINS=true` in the isolated env (harness.ts line 615). This env var controls whether OpenCode discovers default plugins, but the `plugin` array in `opencode.json` is an explicit plugin list that OpenCode still tries to resolve regardless. So the 404 error fires, but it does not actually block startup. OpenCode logs the error and continues. The e2e tests all pass despite this error because the plugin-under-test is wired separately via `.opencode/plugins/opencode-coder.js`.

**Why it still needs fixing**: The error pollutes logs during e2e and manual verification runs. When you are verifying acceptance criteria (like in the lg2.6 acceptance review where this was discovered), spurious `session.error` lines from an unrelated 404 make it harder to spot real problems. This is a test hygiene issue, not a correctness issue.

**Suggested action**: Keep priority 2, but acknowledge this is a noise/hygiene bug, not a blocking defect.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Recommended fix: Remove the plugin entry from shared config, fix it in one place only

**What**: The fix belongs in the shared config file `tests/e2e/fixtures/_shared/opencode-config/opencode.json`. Change the `plugin` array from `["@hk9890/opencode-dynatrace@0.6.0"]` to `[]` (empty array).

**Why**: The shared config's stated purpose (per TESTING.md line 107 and fixtures/README.md line 21) is "provider/model setup matches real local usage during tests." But `@hk9890/opencode-dynatrace` is not a provider/model config — it is a separate plugin that configures Dynatrace-specific behavior. The actual provider/model setup comes from `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT` overrides (used in scenario 5) or from the base config fields like `theme`, `permission`, `autoupdate`, etc. The plugin entry does not contribute to any test assertion in the e2e suite — no test checks for Dynatrace plugin loading. It only exists because the config was likely snapshotted from the developer's real config.

**Why NOT in the harness or fixture setup**: The harness code (`createIsolatedOpenCodePaths` at line 600) does a raw `cp` of the shared config into isolated `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR`. There is no filtering or patching step. Adding a patching step to strip unavailable plugins would be over-engineered for this — the simpler fix is to not put unavailable plugins in the committed baseline in the first place.

**Suggested action**: 
1. Set `"plugin": []` in `tests/e2e/fixtures/_shared/opencode-config/opencode.json`
2. Update the test assertions in `manual-launcher.test.ts` that currently assert `@hk9890/opencode-dynatrace@0.6.0` is present (lines 50, 209, 279, 402) — these should assert the plugin array is empty or only contains expected entries
3. Update `readSharedProviderPluginSpecs()` in harness.ts (line 196-201) — it filters the fixture config for non-coder plugins. With an empty array, it returns empty, which is correct for `installed-configured` mode
4. Update the documentation in TESTING.md line 107 and fixtures/README.md line 21 that describe this plugin as intentionally present
5. Update test fixtures in `manual-launcher.test.ts` lines 131, 156, 183, 348, 419 that use `@hk9890/opencode-dynatrace@0.6.0` in synthetic host configs — these are testing host config resolution, not the shared fixture, so they can keep the reference as a synthetic test value OR switch to a different placeholder

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Coupling analysis: relationship to p7e and 4yl

**What**: 7a2 has no blocking dependency on p7e or 4yl, but all three share context.

**Why this matters for execution order**:

- **p7e (docs lifecycle commands not observable in launcher command mode)**: p7e is about slash command execution not producing observable output. 7a2's startup error noise is a separate layer — fixing 7a2 will make p7e investigation cleaner (less log noise to filter), but p7e's root cause is unrelated to the dynatrace plugin 404. No dependency.

- **4yl (manual launcher copies live .beads socket from --project-path source)**: 4yl is about the `--project-path` copy failing on socket files. 7a2 is about the `--fixture` path seeding a bad config. They affect different code paths in the harness (`createProjectPathWorkspace` vs `createIsolatedOpenCodePaths`). No dependency.

- **Hidden coupling**: All three bugs were discovered during lg2.6 acceptance review and all affect the reliability of the test/verification infrastructure. If you are planning to fix test infrastructure as a batch, these three can be parallelized — none blocks the other. However, fixing 7a2 first will reduce noise when investigating p7e.

**Suggested action**: No dependency links needed. If batching infra fixes, consider 7a2 first since it is the smallest and reduces noise for the other two.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Description is sufficient to execute, with one clarification needed

**What**: The bug description correctly identifies the problem (shared config references unavailable plugin), provides evidence (log path with exact error), and states the expected behavior. A tasker can execute from this.

**Why one clarification matters**: The description says the config "should either avoid enabling unavailable external plugins in this test baseline, or provide a deterministic install path." The second option (deterministic install path) is a trap — `@hk9890/opencode-dynatrace` is a private/unpublished package. There is no install path to provide. The only viable fix direction is option 1: remove the plugin from the test baseline. The description should not suggest the install-path option as equally valid because a tasker might waste time exploring it.

title: Manual launcher copies live .beads socket from --project-path source
description: Discovered while verifying opencode-coder-lg2.6. Running the documented manual launcher with --project-path against the repo root failed before verification because the source copy includes a live .beads/bd.sock socket file, and Bun cp aborts with: cannot copy a socket file: <temp>/project/.beads/bd.sock. This blocks acceptance-style manual validation on real project paths and makes the documented --project-path workflow unreliable for active beads repos. Expected behavior: the launcher should exclude transient socket files like .beads/bd.sock (and likely other runtime sockets) when copying external projects, similar to its exclusion of .git contents, so copy-based reproduction can proceed safely.
close_reason: Updated manual launcher project-path copy filter to exclude .git/.beads/.coder and added regression test coverage with live .beads socket + runtime-state assertions.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Verdict: Confirmed real bug — the filter logic is clearly incomplete

**What**: The `shouldCopyPath` function in `tests/e2e/helpers/harness.ts` (line 474-482) only excludes `.git` segments from the copy. When `--project-path` targets an active beads repo, `fs/promises.cp` encounters `.beads/bd.sock` (a Unix domain socket) and aborts because Node/Bun `cp` cannot copy socket files. This is deterministic — any active beads repo will hit it.

**Why**: This blocks the primary use case of `--project-path`: validating the plugin against real, active project trees. It's not a rare edge case — it's the normal state of any repo where `bd` is running. The existing e2e test for `--project-path` (line 289-339 in `manual-launcher.test.ts`) only creates a minimal synthetic source with `.git/` and `README.md`, so it never exercises the socket-file path and doesn't catch this.

**Suggested action**: No action needed on this comment — it confirms the bug is real and correctly filed. See subsequent comments for fix direction.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Other transient runtime files to consider beyond bd.sock

**What**: Inspecting a live `.beads/` directory reveals these additional transient/runtime files that should never be copied:

| File | Type | Why exclude |
|------|------|-------------|
| `bd.sock` | Unix socket | Direct blocker — cp aborts on sockets |
| `daemon.pid` | PID file | Stale PID, meaningless in copy |
| `daemon.lock` | Lock file | Stale lock, meaningless in copy |
| `daemon.log` | Log (~40MB) | Large, runtime-only |
| `dolt-server.pid` | PID file | Stale PID |
| `dolt-server.lock` | Lock file | Stale lock |
| `dolt-server.port` | Port file | Stale port binding |
| `dolt-server.log` | Log (~112MB) | Very large, runtime-only |
| `dolt-server.activity` | Activity marker | Runtime-only |
| `dolt-monitor.pid.lock` | Lock file | Stale lock |
| `dolt/` | Database dir | Live database state |

**Why**: Even if we only fix `bd.sock`, the other files cause the copy to take much longer than necessary (150MB+ of logs alone) and produce a workspace with stale daemon state that could confuse debugging. Excluding the entire `.beads` directory is the correct granularity — there is no valid reason to copy any of it into an isolated test workspace.

**Suggested action**: Exclude `.beads` as a whole directory (not individual files). If a future test needs beads state, it should be set up intentionally via `bd init` or a purpose-built fixture, not by copying live daemon state.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Fix directly as a bug — do not convert to task

**What**: This should be fixed as-is (bug), not converted to a task. The scope is minimal: one function change in `shouldCopyPath`, plus an updated or new e2e test assertion that verifies socket-containing source directories are handled correctly.

**Why**: (1) The fix is a 3-line function edit with zero architectural implications. (2) It has no external API surface — it's internal test harness code. (3) Converting to a task adds ceremony (acceptance criteria, planning) that exceeds the complexity of the work. (4) The test gap should be closed in the same PR: the existing `--project-path` test (line 289) should add a socket file to the synthetic source to prevent regression.

**Suggested action**: Fix in-place as this bug. The complete scope is:
1. Update `shouldCopyPath` to exclude `.beads` and `.coder` segments
2. Extract the exclusion list into a named constant for clarity
3. Add a socket file (via `net.createServer` or similar) to the `--project-path` test's synthetic source to verify the filter works
4. Consider adding a `.beads/daemon.pid` or similar to the test source to verify the whole directory is excluded, not just sockets

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Bug description is sufficient but should mention .coder/ exclusion

**What**: The bug description correctly identifies the root cause (socket copy failure), the affected code path (--project-path workflow), and the expected behavior (exclude transient files). It mentions "and likely other runtime sockets" which is directionally correct. However, it does not mention `.coder/` as another directory that should be excluded for isolation correctness.

**Why**: The description is good enough to implement from — a tasker would find the right code. But the `.coder/` exclusion is a correctness concern beyond the crash fix, and omitting it means the implementer might not think about it.

**Suggested action**: No description edit needed (per review rules, I don't modify issue content). The fix recommendations in the comments above cover the full scope including `.coder/`. The implementer should read all comments before starting.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text: Reviewer conclusion: confirmed real launcher bug. The copy filter used by the manual launcher should exclude transient runtime directories such as `.beads` and `.coder`, not just `.git`. This avoids copying live socket files like `.beads/bd.sock` and avoids leaking runtime state into isolated workspaces. Expected fix direction: direct implementation against this bug in the manual launcher/test harness, plus regression coverage.

title: Document manual validation scenarios for docs lifecycle acceptance
description:
## Description
Close the remaining acceptance gap for the docs lifecycle epic by adding explicit manual validation coverage for the functional scenarios that are not deterministic to automate end-to-end.

## Why
The remaining gap in `opencode-coder-e3v` is not primarily a product bug; it is a validation gap. We already have automated coverage for command registration, runtime gating, and template alignment. What is still missing is precise manual validation guidance for the AI-agent-mediated scenarios.

## Addresses
- `opencode-coder-e3v`

## Instructions
1. Update `docs/TESTING.md` so the docs lifecycle section contains explicit manual validation scenarios for:
   - team-mode `/opencode-coder/docs`
   - stealth-mode `/opencode-coder/docs`
   - `/opencode-coder/init` delegating into docs lifecycle
   - `/opencode-coder/improve-doc` with an incident such as missing `validate-before-release.sh`
2. For each scenario, define:
   - starting repository/mode state
   - exact command(s) to run
   - the expected observable outcomes
   - what evidence to capture if the behavior is wrong
3. Ensure the guidance clearly distinguishes:
   - deterministic automated coverage already provided by unit/integration/e2e tests
   - manual validation required for agent-mediated functional behavior
4. Add or update any nearby test docs if needed so future maintainers know how to re-run these validations during acceptance review.
5. Keep scope focused on validation/documentation unless you discover a genuine product issue while validating. If you do, create a follow-up bug instead of broadening this task.

## Files to Modify
- `docs/TESTING.md`
- other nearby docs only if needed for validation clarity

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `docs/TESTING.md` contains explicit manual validation scenarios for the remaining docs lifecycle acceptance cases
- [ ] Each scenario defines setup, command, expected outcomes, and failure evidence
- [ ] The guidance makes clear which parts are automated vs manual validation
- [ ] The resulting manual validation plan is sufficient for a verifier to re-run acceptance intentionally
close_reason: Added explicit manual docs lifecycle acceptance scenarios in docs/TESTING.md, including setup, commands, expected outcomes, and failure evidence, with clear automated-vs-manual distinction.

title: Docs lifecycle acceptance scenarios lack functional execution coverage
description:
Discovered while verifying opencode-coder-lg2.6.

## What is missing
Current automated/manual verification covers command registration and file structure, but not the functional scenario behavior required by the acceptance review.

## Evidence
Passing tests today verify:
- package/file registration contracts (tests/unit/docs-lifecycle-contract.test.ts)
- command exposure by mode (tests/integration/plugin.test.ts)
- command names on real startup paths (tests/e2e/opencode.test.ts scenarios 1-4)

What is still not executed end-to-end:
- team-mode /opencode-coder/docs behavior (routing releases/monitoring to skills, refreshing existing CODING.md, no hollow docs, created/updated/skipped/routed reporting)
- stealth-mode /opencode-coder/docs behavior (write only under .coder paths, preserve root AGENTS.md)
- init delegating into the shared docs lifecycle
- incident-driven /opencode-coder/improve-doc mapping a failure to the right doc/routing/skill update

The manual validation section added to docs/TESTING.md also checks command visibility, not these behaviors.

## Why this matters
Acceptance criterion 9 requires the functional scenarios to be covered well enough by code/tests/docs. Current coverage is not sufficient to prove those behaviors.
close_reason: Stale umbrella issue: automated registration coverage was fixed by opencode-coder-3fr and manual functional validation guidance was added by opencode-coder-2y5/5vx. Remaining executable blockers are tracked concretely in opencode-coder-y89 and opencode-coder-2jk.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## This is a test gap bug, not a product bug — and its scope is too broad to execute as-is

**What**: The bug lists four missing functional scenarios (team-mode docs, stealth-mode docs, init delegation, incident-driven improvement). But these are AI-agent-mediated workflows — the "behavior" being tested is an LLM following markdown instructions. You can't write a deterministic unit test that verifies "AGENTS.md routes releases to skills instead of creating hollow docs" because that's an emergent behavior of the agent interpreting the command template.

**Why**: The acceptance criteria (criterion 9) says "functional scenarios covered well enough by code/tests/docs." The key phrase is "well enough." The existing test pyramid already covers: (a) command registration contracts, (b) command exposure by mode, (c) file existence contracts, (d) runtime startup behavior. What's actually missing is documented manual validation scenarios for the behavior that can only be tested by running the commands with a real agent. Creating deterministic automated tests for LLM-mediated behavior will either be flaky or trivially tautological.

**Suggested action**: Split this into two concrete deliverables:
1. **Automated**: Add integration tests for the resource-gating gap identified in opencode-coder-gq1 (command exposure depends on resource availability). This IS deterministically testable.
2. **Manual validation doc**: Expand `docs/TESTING.md` with explicit manual validation scenarios for each functional scenario (A-D). Define the exact fixture setup, the command to run, and the expected observable outcomes. This is the appropriate test level for agent-mediated behavior.

Do NOT attempt to automate the full functional scenarios. The ROI is negative.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Verdict: e3v should be closeable once 3fr is fixed and manual validation is confirmed adequate

**What**: e3v says "docs lifecycle acceptance scenarios lack functional execution coverage." There are two types of coverage missing:
1. Automated e2e coverage for command registration in the team-mode startup path (this is actually what 3fr blocks — scenario 1 would prove docs commands appear in active team mode if the fixture were correct)
2. Functional agent-mediated behavior coverage for scenarios A-D (team docs lifecycle behavior, stealth docs lifecycle behavior, init delegation, incident-driven improvement)

For item 1: fixing the fixture in 3fr directly proves the automated command-registration gap is closed. Once scenario 1 passes, automated coverage verifies that active team mode exposes docs lifecycle commands via real server startup.

For item 2: the existing comment on e3v (019d1675-b773) is correct — these are AI-agent-mediated workflows. You cannot write deterministic automated tests for "AGENTS.md routes releases to skills instead of creating hollow docs" because that is emergent LLM behavior following markdown instructions. The closed task opencode-coder-2y5 added manual validation scenarios to docs/TESTING.md for exactly this purpose. That IS the right coverage level for agent-mediated behavior.

**Why**: e3v conflates two problems: (a) a fixture bug blocking automated e2e verification (which is 3fr), and (b) a philosophical gap about how to test agent-mediated command behavior. Problem (a) has a concrete fix. Problem (b) was already addressed by 2y5 with manual validation guidance — the acceptance criteria just need to acknowledge that manual validation IS sufficient for agent-mediated behavior.

**Suggested action**: After 3fr is fixed and scenario 1 passes, verify that docs/TESTING.md manual validation scenarios are adequate for acceptance scenarios A-D. If they are, close e3v with a note explaining that automated command-registration coverage now passes (via scenario 1) and functional agent-mediated behavior is covered by documented manual validation. Do not attempt to automate the agent-mediated scenarios.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text: Reviewer analysis: this bug should be closable once opencode-coder-3fr is fixed. Automated gap is scenario-1 e2e coverage; remaining agent-mediated behavior is already covered by explicit manual validation scenarios in docs/TESTING.md from opencode-coder-2y5.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Verdict: e3v is a stale umbrella issue that should be closed — its two sub-problems are now fully addressed by other issues

**What**: e3v originally identified two gaps: (1) automated e2e coverage for docs lifecycle command registration, and (2) functional agent-mediated behavioral coverage for scenarios A-D. Both gaps are now resolved by other work:

1. **Automated e2e gap**: Fixed. opencode-coder-3fr (closed) fixed the fixture. E2E scenario 1 now passes — confirmed by running bun test tests/e2e/opencode.test.ts --test-name-pattern "scenario 1" just now (1 pass, 0 fail, 2.3s). Integration tests verify command exposure across all four modes (inactive/disabled/team/stealth). Unit tests verify lifecycle contracts. The automated coverage gap described in e3v no longer exists.

2. **Manual functional behavioral gap**: Addressed. opencode-coder-2y5 (closed) added 4 explicit manual validation scenarios to docs/TESTING.md (lines 402-516) covering team-mode docs, stealth-mode docs, init delegation, and incident-driven improvement. Each scenario specifies starting state, commands, expected outcomes, and failure evidence. The prior comment on e3v (019d1675) correctly identified that these are agent-mediated workflows where manual validation IS the appropriate test level.

e3v has no remaining original problem that is not already tracked elsewhere. It is not a bug — it was always a test gap observation that spawned concrete work items.

**Why**: Keeping e3v open creates confusion. Three reviewers across multiple sessions have independently concluded it should be closeable. The comments on e3v already say this (comments 019d1694 and 019d1695). The only reason it stayed open was 3fr blocking scenario 1 — that blocker is now closed and the test passes. e3v has no acceptance criteria of its own that are not covered by the combination of (a) passing e2e/integration/unit tests and (b) documented manual validation in TESTING.md.

**Suggested action**: Close e3v with close reason: "Both sub-problems resolved: automated e2e registration coverage now passes via 3fr fixture fix (scenario 1 green), and manual functional validation is documented in docs/TESTING.md via 2y5. No remaining original gap."

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## e3v was never a bug — it was a test gap observation misclassified as type=bug

**What**: The original description says "Current automated/manual verification covers command registration and file structure, but not the functional scenario behavior required by the acceptance review." This is an observation about test coverage adequacy during acceptance review. It is not a product defect. No code is broken. No user-facing behavior is wrong. The "bug" is that the test pyramid did not yet cover certain scenarios at the time of filing.

**Why**: Classifying test coverage gaps as bugs conflates "the product is broken" with "we have not proven the product works." These are different problems requiring different responses. A bug gets fixed by changing product code. A test gap gets fixed by adding tests or documentation. All the work that addressed e3v (3fr, 2y5, 67d, a82) confirms this — the product code changes (67d, a82) were about gating and template alignment, not fixing the behaviors e3v describes. The test/doc additions (3fr, 2y5) were about proving coverage, not fixing behavior.

**Suggested action**: If e3v were to stay open (it should not — see other comment), it should be type=task, not type=bug. But the better action is to close it since all its concrete deliverables are done.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Dependency/order analysis: e3v vs y89, 2jk, and lg2.6

**What**: The relationship between e3v and the three named issues is:

1. **opencode-coder-y89** (open, P1): Manual launcher --project-path copies lose active mode markers. This is a REAL blocker for manual acceptance validation of scenarios A/B/C. It is NOT related to e3v. y89 blocks the ability to USE the manual validation documented in TESTING.md. e3v was about whether that documentation EXISTS. The docs exist (via 2y5). The tooling to execute them is broken (via y89). These are orthogonal problems.

2. **opencode-coder-2jk** (open, P2): Broken symlinks in .opencode/commands. This pollutes manual launcher evidence with ENOENT noise. It is a development-environment hygiene bug. It does not block e3v closure — it is a separate, independent quality issue that affects ALL manual launcher runs, not just docs lifecycle ones.

3. **opencode-coder-lg2.6** (in_progress): The acceptance review task. lg2.6 criteria 6-8 (team/stealth/incident functional scenarios) cannot be EXECUTED until y89 is fixed. But the structural criteria (1-5, 9, 10) are passing. e3v was discovered-from lg2.6 but is no longer blocking it — the test gap e3v identified is now filled. What blocks lg2.6 completion is y89 (cannot run the manual validation) and potentially 2jk (noisy evidence).

**Why**: e3v should not be kept open as a proxy for "manual validation still cannot be executed." That problem is y89, and y89 already exists with the correct problem statement. Keeping e3v open alongside y89 creates two issues tracking different aspects of the same acceptance completion problem — confusing for anyone triaging the open issue list.

**Suggested action**: 
- Close e3v (test gap is documented, automated coverage passes)
- y89 is the real remaining blocker for lg2.6 functional acceptance — it stays open at P1
- 2jk stays open at P2 — it is independent cleanup
- lg2.6 acceptance completion depends on: y89 fixed, then re-run manual scenarios, then close lg2.6

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## What should replace e3v in beads reality

**What**: After closing e3v, the remaining open issues in the docs lifecycle acceptance space are:

1. **opencode-coder-y89** (P1 bug): The only real blocker for lg2.6 functional acceptance. Fix the launcher to preserve .coder/ mode markers during --project-path copy. This is the concrete, executable problem.
2. **opencode-coder-2jk** (P2 bug): Development hygiene — remove or fix broken symlinks in .opencode/commands. Independent of acceptance.
3. **opencode-coder-lg2.6** (P1 acceptance task): Waiting on y89. Once y89 is fixed, re-run manual scenarios 1-4 from TESTING.md, record evidence, and close.

No new issues need to be created. The problem space that e3v vaguely covered is now precisely modeled by these three concrete issues.

**Why**: e3v's description mixes four different problems (team-mode behavior, stealth-mode behavior, init delegation, incident improvement) into one issue with no acceptance criteria of its own. The replacement model — passing automated tests + documented manual validation scenarios + y89 as the execution blocker — is more precise and actionable.

**Suggested action**: Close e3v. The path to closing the epic is: fix y89 -> execute manual scenarios -> close lg2.6 -> close lg2 epic. Optionally fix 2jk to reduce launcher noise.

title: Add an incident-driven improve-doc command
description:
## Description
Add a second command for targeted documentation improvement when something went wrong because local guidance was missing, unclear, outdated, or routed incorrectly.

## Why
`/opencode-coder/docs` is the main lifecycle command. But we also want a focused command for cases like:
- "we forgot to run validate-before-release.sh"
- "the docs didn't explain the right release step"
- "AGENTS routed to the wrong place"

This command should learn from the failure and propose changes that prevent recurrence.

## Command model
Keep this as a separate command:
- `ai-resources/commands/opencode-coder/improve-doc.md`

It should still reuse the shared lifecycle reference rather than duplicating lifecycle logic.

## Instructions
1. Create `/opencode-coder/improve-doc` as a thin dispatcher that uses the incident-improvement section of `project-docs-lifecycle.md`.
2. Define the input contract explicitly:
   - optional free-text argument describing what went wrong
   - optional issue/reference identifier to pull context from a tracked bug/task
   - if no useful input is provided, prompt the user for failure context
3. Support examples such as:
   - `/opencode-coder/improve-doc "forgot to run validate-before-release.sh"`
   - `/opencode-coder/improve-doc --issue <id>` or equivalent issue-reference pattern
4. The workflow must identify whether the missing or weak guidance belongs in:
   - a project doc
   - AGENTS routing
   - the opencode-coder skill/reference
   - or some combination
5. The workflow must analyze why the current docs/routing did not prevent the issue.
6. The workflow must propose updates aimed at preventing recurrence.
7. This command is **not** for generic typo/grammar cleanup.

## Files to Modify
- `ai-resources/commands/opencode-coder/improve-doc.md` (create)
- `ai-resources/skills/opencode-coder/SKILL.md`
- `ai-resources/skills/opencode-coder/references/project-docs-lifecycle.md`
- related opencode-coder references as needed

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A targeted improve-doc command exists
- [ ] The command has an explicit input contract (text, issue/reference, or prompt fallback)
- [ ] The command can map a failure/omission to the right doc, routing, or skill gap
- [ ] The command focuses on recurrence prevention, not generic editorial cleanup
- [ ] The lifecycle reference explains how incident-driven improvement reuses the shared docs model
close_reason: Implemented /opencode-coder/improve-doc as a thin dispatcher with explicit incident input contract, shared lifecycle incident-improvement section, and discoverability updates.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## improve-doc needs a concrete input format, not just "failure context"

**What**: The task says the command "should accept failure context such as: 'we forgot to run validate-before-release.sh'". But it doesn't specify how. Is this a command argument? A free-text prompt? A beads issue ID? Does the user paste a log? The command's UX is undefined.

**Why**: Without a defined input contract, the tasker will have to invent one. The resulting command might work well for one input shape and poorly for others. The acceptance criteria can't be verified without knowing what "takes failure/omission context" looks like concretely.

**Suggested action**: Define the input model explicitly. Recommendation:
- The command takes an optional text argument describing what went wrong
- If no argument, the command prompts the user with `question()` for failure context

title: Retire fix-documentation and move doc fix/update guidance into opencode-coder
description:
## Description
Stop using `fix-documentation` for project-document lifecycle work and make `opencode-coder` the single home for creating, fixing, updating, auditing, slimming, and improving project docs.

## Why
You explicitly decided that documentation lifecycle work should live in the opencode-coder plugin/skill. We therefore should not continue to send agents to `fix-documentation` for project-doc lifecycle work.

## Scope clarification
The current `fix-documentation` skill is repo-local at:
- `.opencode/skills/fix-documentation/`

This task is **not** about publishing that skill.
It is about retiring or redirecting its lifecycle responsibility in this repo and moving the important guidance into `opencode-coder`.

## Instructions
1. Decide and document that `opencode-coder` owns the full project-doc lifecycle for initialized projects:
   - setup
   - create
   - fix
   - update
   - audit
   - slim/split
   - improve after failures
2. Review `.opencode/skills/fix-documentation/` and identify the parts that should move into `opencode-coder`.

   - project documentation synchronization workflow
   - AGENTS-specific maintenance workflow
   - doc verification guidance such as links/commands/cross-reference checks
4. Keep only truly generic editorial functionality in `fix-documentation` **if** anything remains useful there.
5. If `.opencode/skills/fix-documentation/` remains in the repo, mark it clearly as deprecated or redirect it to `opencode-coder` for lifecycle work.
6. Remove any repo guidance that still suggests using `fix-documentation` for project-doc lifecycle work.

- `ai-resources/skills/opencode-coder/references/project-docs-lifecycle.md`
- `.opencode/skills/fix-documentation/SKILL.md`

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## fix-documentation overlap is already real and concrete — this task should name the specific conflicts

**What**: The task says "Remove overlapping or misleading guidance where both skills claim the same lifecycle responsibility." But it doesn't identify what those overlaps are. Having read both skills, the specific overlaps are:
1. `fix-documentation` Workflow 3 ("Fix AGENTS.md Specifically") directly overlaps with the new docs lifecycle command's AGENTS maintenance role
2. `fix-documentation` Workflow 2 ("Fix Project Documentation") audits and syncs README/CONTRIBUTING/AGENTS — this overlaps with the docs lifecycle command's audit/repair flow
3. `fix-documentation` has its own mode detection logic that duplicates `project-structure.md`

**Why**: Without naming the specific conflicts, the tasker will spend time rediscovering them. Worse, they might miss some and leave stale overlapping guidance in place.

**Suggested action**: Add the specific conflicts to the task instructions:
- `fix-documentation` Workflow 2 (project documentation sync) → fold the useful parts (command verification, cross-reference checking) into the docs lifecycle reference, remove the rest
- `fix-documentation` Workflow 3 (AGENTS.md fix) → fully superseded by the docs lifecycle command, remove or redirect
- `fix-documentation` Workflow 1 (single file fix) → this is the keeper, it's genuinely different from lifecycle management
- Mode detection in `fix-documentation` references → should defer to `project-structure.md` rather than duplicating it

title: Document bug reproduction and installed-vs-local comparison workflows
description:
## Description
Document how to perform reproducible installed-vs-local comparisons and how to use the harness for general bug reproduction and "is this already fixed?" verification.

## Instructions
1. Update `docs/TESTING.md` to distinguish integration tests from real CLI/manual issue reproduction.
2. Document both project-source modes: committed fixtures and external project paths copied into temp workspaces.
3. Document both plugin-source modes: local-build and installed-configured.
4. Add concrete command examples for comparing the same project with installed and local plugin sources, including preserved-temp-workspace debugging flows.
5. Clarify the safety model and limits: external project copy behavior, host config only used to resolve installed package specs, and the fact that exact in-place reproduction is out of scope for this iteration.
6. Add a short workflow for: reproduce issue with installed version -> rerun with local build -> decide whether current implementation already fixes the issue.
7. Add a simple decision matrix for when to use integration tests, fixture-based e2e/manual runs, or external-project reproduction.
8. Update nearby docs such as `tests/e2e/fixtures/README.md` if fixture-specific clarification is needed.

## Files to Modify
- `docs/TESTING.md` — add workflow and comparison guidance
- `tests/e2e/fixtures/README.md` — clarify fixture vs external-project workflows if needed

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Docs show a repeatable external-project investigation workflow
- [ ] Docs show installed-vs-local comparison commands
- [ ] Docs clearly state that integration tests do not cover real CLI startup hangs or other real project reproduction cases
- [ ] Docs include a clear "is this already fixed in current code?" workflow
- [ ] Docs include a decision matrix for choosing the right test/reproduction mode
- [ ] Docs match implemented launcher flags and defaults exactly
close_reason: Updated testing docs with decision matrix, installed-vs-local comparison workflow, project/plugin source modes, safety limits, and fixture README clarifications; validated against launcher help and preflight tests.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Docs task should include a decision matrix, not just command examples

**What**: The task instructions list "distinguish integration tests from real CLI/manual issue reproduction" and "add concrete command examples" but don't require a clear decision matrix that helps someone choose the right approach for their situation.

**Why**: The real user question isn't "what commands exist" — it's "I have a bug report. Which tool do I use?" Without a decision matrix (e.g., "use unit tests for X, integration tests for Y, manual reproduction for Z"), the docs will be a reference that nobody consults because they don't know which section applies to them.

**Suggested action**: Add to instructions: "Include a decision matrix or flowchart at the top of the new section: given a bug report, how do you decide between (a) writing a unit/integration test, (b) using the manual launcher with a fixture, (c) using the manual launcher with an external project, and (d) using installed-configured mode for regression checking. Keep it to ~5-8 rows maximum."

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Docs task acceptance criteria are not verifiable without the implementation

**What**: Every acceptance criterion is phrased as "Docs show X" or "Docs match implemented launcher flags." But the docs task depends on tasks 1 and 2, meaning a tasker writing docs must have the final flag names, defaults, and output format already implemented. If task 1 or 2 changes flag names during implementation, the docs are immediately stale.

**Why**: This is a common sequencing trap. The docs task can't be verified independently — it's coupled to implementation details that may shift. This isn't a plan flaw, but the tasker needs to know.

**Suggested action**: Add a note to the instructions: "This task should be implemented after tasks .1 and .2 are merged. Use the actual implemented `--help` output and test results as the source of truth for flag names and defaults. Do not invent flag names — read them from the code." This is implicit from the dependency graph but worth stating explicitly so the tasker doesn't start early with placeholder names.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## This bug is a symptom of 874, not independent — but the test gap is real and needs its own fix

**What**: Bug 316 says the test at manual-launcher.test.ts passes despite the env isolation being broken. This is true: lines 60-66 assert presence of isolation markers (`OPENCODE_DISABLE_DEFAULT_PLUGINS=true`, `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR=`) but never assert absence of host pollution. The test would pass even if the child env contained every secret on the host. However, this bug only matters because 874 exists — once 874's env allowlist fix lands, the child env will be minimal by construction, and host env leakage becomes impossible without a code regression.

**Why**: The test gap still needs closing even after 874 is fixed, because tests should guard the contract, not rely on the implementation being correct. If someone later adds a "convenience" passthrough that re-introduces `...process.env`, the existing test would still pass. The test needs a negative assertion.

**Suggested action**: After the 874 fix lands, add assertions to the existing test that verify env minimality. The right approach is NOT to enumerate every forbidden var (that's fragile). Instead:

1. Count the total env vars in the child output — with the allowlist approach from 874, the child env should have roughly 10-15 vars. Assert `envVarCount < 25` (generous upper bound). If someone sneaks `...process.env` back in, the count jumps to 150+ and the test fails.
2. Spot-check that specific known-dangerous host vars are absent: assert stdout does NOT contain patterns like `JIRA_TOKEN=`, `npm_lifecycle_script=`, `KITTY_PID=`. These are canaries — if any of them appear, host env leaked.

This approach is both robust and self-documenting. The count assertion catches bulk leakage; the canary assertions catch targeted leakage.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Consider merging 316 into the 874 fix instead of keeping them separate

**What**: Bug 316 is "test doesn't catch env leakage" and bug 874 is "env leaks." Fixing 874 without also fixing 316 means the regression guard is missing. Fixing 316 without fixing 874 means the test will fail (which is correct behavior but means 316 blocks on 874 anyway). These two bugs should be fixed in the same PR.

**Why**: Splitting them into separate PRs creates an ordering dependency that adds no value. The 874 fix changes the env construction; the 316 fix adds assertions that verify the new env construction. They're two halves of the same change. Merging them reduces review overhead and eliminates the window where the fix is live but unguarded.

**Suggested action**: Implement 874 and 316 together. The PR should:
1. Change the env construction to allowlist (874)
2. Add env-minimality assertions to manual-launcher.test.ts (316)
3. Verify TUI mode still works (manual smoke)
4. Update TESTING.md to document the allowlist policy

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## The launcher's test also has the same env leak pattern in runLauncher()

**What**: The test file `manual-launcher.test.ts` lines 13-15 constructs its own env for running the launcher process as `{ ...process.env, PATH: process.env.PATH ?? "" }`. This is the same `...process.env` antipattern. However, this one is less critical because it's the env for the launcher process itself (which then constructs the child env). Once the launcher's child env is fixed (874), the test's launcher-process env doesn't matter for isolation — the launcher will strip it before passing to the child. But it's still sloppy and worth noting: the test runner inherits the full host env, which means the launcher's `process.env` (which it uses to read `SHELL`, check `PATH`, etc.) contains host state. This is fine for the launcher's own logic but the implementer should be aware that `process.env.SHELL` on line 351 reads from the test's inherited env, not from a controlled env.

**Why**: This is a code hygiene observation, not a blocking issue. The launcher reads `process.env.SHELL` and `process.env.PATH` for its own operation before constructing the child env — that's fine. But if anyone later adds `process.env.SOME_VAR` to the child env thinking "the launcher has it," they'll re-break isolation. The env construction should use `process.env` for reading launcher-config values and `isolatedPaths.env` + explicit allowlist for the child.

**Suggested action**: No code change needed — just be aware of the asymmetry. A code comment at the child env construction point would help: `// Child env is intentionally stripped. Use allowlist, not process.env spread.`

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text: Reviewer summary: this bug should be fixed together with the root env-isolation bug. Current automated verification only checks for presence of isolated env markers, not absence of host pollution. Update the launcher tests to assert env-minimality / no host OPENCODE_* leakage, and ensure interactive-oriented mode still gets needed terminal vars.

title: Manual launcher auth-path preflight prints raw stack trace
description:
## Summary
Passing a missing auth path to the manual launcher does not produce a friendly preflight error. The process throws from shared harness code and prints a Bun stack trace instead.

## Evidence
Running:

a\) bun run test:manual -- --mode=command --fixture=cli-smoke-project --auth=/tmp/does-not-exist-auth.json -- env

Observed:
- uncaught exception from tests/e2e/helpers/harness.ts
- Bun stack trace shown to the user
- no launcher-level friendly message like the argument parser and unknown-fixture path provide

## Impact
This does not meet the human-friendly preflight/error expectation for manual use.

## Expected
The launcher should catch invalid auth seed path resolution and print a concise human-facing error, similar to other preflight failures.
close_reason: Moved --auth seed-path resolution into guarded preflight handling so invalid auth paths return concise user-facing error without Bun stack trace.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
Hans Kohlreiter
Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text: Reviewer summary: independent UX bug. resolveAuthSeedPath() is called before the launcher's try/catch, so invalid --auth paths throw through Bun and print a raw stack trace. Recommended fix: move auth resolution into a guarded preflight path and return a concise human-facing error like the existing argument/fixture checks.

title: Audit: opencode-coder skill — validation findings
description:
## Description
Full validation audit of the opencode-coder skill (ai-resources/skills/opencode-coder/).

Evaluated: trigger description quality, internal consistency, correctness/actionability of workflows, structure, missing/stale/contradictory guidance, and bundled resource usage.

## Scope
- SKILL.md (hub)
- 10 reference docs in references/
- 1 script in scripts/
- 1 asset in assets/

## Summary
The skill is well-structured as a lazy-load reference hub with 10 focused reference docs. Most workflows are actionable and internally consistent. However, there are several stale references to beads internals that no longer exist, a non-existent `bd stats` command reference, ambiguous script paths in bug-reporting.md, and the trigger description is overloaded. See comments for individual findings.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## [HIGH] Stale reference: beads.db does not exist in Dolt-backed beads

**What**: troubleshooting-patterns.md (lines 214, 423-424, 429, 443) and project-structure.md (line 56) reference beads.db as a SQLite cache that can be deleted to fix database errors. The actual beads install uses Dolt (.beads/dolt/), and there is no beads.db file. The troubleshooting advice "rm .beads/beads.db" will do nothing, and the gitignore guidance about excluding beads.db is misleading.

**Why**: An agent or user following this troubleshooting advice will think they fixed a database corruption issue when they haven't. The actual Dolt data directory is never mentioned. This is the most-used troubleshooting pattern and it is wrong.

**Suggested action**: 
1. Replace beads.db references with current Dolt-based architecture. The cache rebuild may now be bd doctor --fix or similar.
2. Update project-structure.md line 56 to exclude the actual runtime files (daemon.*, *.lock, etc.) rather than a nonexistent beads.db.
3. Verify with bd doctor output what the current cache/rebuild mechanism is.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## [HIGH] Non-existent command: bd stats referenced in planning.md

**What**: planning.md line 265 says "Show the plan: bd stats, bd ready, bd blocked". The bd stats command does not exist in the current bd CLI (verified via bd --help). The correct command is bd status.

**Why**: An agent following the Planning workflow Phase 5 will fail when it runs bd stats. This is a workflow-critical command in the planning reference — the main skill workflow for the planner role.

**Suggested action**: Replace bd stats with bd status on line 265 of planning.md.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## [HIGH] Stale reference: interactions.jsonl in troubleshooting-patterns.md

**What**: troubleshooting-patterns.md line 358 instructs agents to run: cat .beads/interactions.jsonl | tail -20 for debugging agent behavior. This file does not exist in the current beads installation. bd doctor lists it among files that should be untracked/ignored, confirming it is a legacy artifact.

**Why**: An agent following this troubleshooting step will get a file-not-found error and have no fallback. The agent-behavior troubleshooting section becomes a dead end.

**Suggested action**: Remove or replace this command with the actual mechanism for inspecting recent beads interactions. If no equivalent exists in Dolt-backed beads, remove the command and note that interaction history is available through Dolt versioning or bd query commands.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## [MEDIUM] Trigger description is overloaded — likely over-triggers

**What**: The SKILL.md description field (line 3) lists 9 numbered trigger conditions spanning planning, simplifying, installing, configuring, debugging, log analysis, health checks, bug reporting, and troubleshooting. This is essentially "load this skill for anything related to the plugin." The description is 449 characters — a wall of text that a trigger-matcher must parse.

**Why**: Over-triggering wastes context window by loading a hub document when the agent may not need the skill at all. For example, a simple bd create command doesn't need the full skill loaded — the agent likely already has AGENTS.md beads instructions. The description also conflates the hub role (route to sub-documents) with the actual sub-workflows, making it hard to distinguish when the skill is genuinely needed vs when AGENTS.md suffices.

**Suggested action**: 
1. Narrow the trigger to situations where the agent explicitly needs plugin-specific workflow guidance that goes beyond basic bd usage already in AGENTS.md.
2. Consider: "Use when the AI assistant needs plugin-specific workflows: planning epics/tasks, simplifying code, initializing or configuring the plugin, debugging plugin issues, or reporting plugin bugs. Not needed for basic bd commands — those are covered by AGENTS.md."
3. Alternatively, split the skill into 2-3 focused skills (e.g., opencode-coder-plan, opencode-coder-ops) to reduce context loading.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## [MEDIUM] collect-system-info.sh references .beads/config.yaml mode field — stale

**What**: scripts/collect-system-info.sh line 29 runs: cat .beads/config.yaml 2>/dev/null | grep mode. But the mode is stored in .coder/opencode-coder.yaml, not .beads/config.yaml. The .beads/config.yaml exists but does not contain a mode field — it contains beads daemon/server configuration.

**Why**: The script is referenced by bug-reporting.md (lines 85, 234) as the way to collect system info for bug reports. Running it will output "Mode: unknown" for every user, making the collected info misleading.

**Suggested action**: Update the script to read mode from .coder/opencode-coder.yaml. Also check for the stealth marker in .git/info/exclude as a fallback, consistent with project-structure.md detection rules.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## [MEDIUM] Ambiguous script paths in bug-reporting.md

**What**: bug-reporting.md lines 85 and 234 reference ./scripts/collect-system-info.sh. This relative path assumes execution from the skill directory root, but the user/agent is in the project working directory. The script lives at ai-resources/skills/opencode-coder/scripts/collect-system-info.sh or .opencode/skills/opencode-coder/scripts/collect-system-info.sh — neither matches ./scripts/.

Similarly, line 231 uses cp ../assets/bug-report-template.md /tmp/bug-report.md — this relative path only works if CWD is references/, which it won't be.

**Why**: An agent or user following the Detailed Report Pattern will fail to find the script and template. The paths are unreachable from the project root where commands are actually executed.

**Suggested action**: 
1. Use absolute paths relative to the skill root, or provide a note that these paths are relative to the skill directory.
2. Better: have the AI agent read the files using its tools rather than telling users to cp from skill-internal paths. The asset and script are AI-facing resources, not user-facing CLI tools.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## [MEDIUM] planning.md shows bd update --status=in_progress but AGENTS.md uses --claim

**What**: planning.md line 289 shows bd update <id> --status=in_progress with the comment "# Claim work". But AGENTS.md (the project's own conventions) uses bd update <id> --claim as the atomic claim mechanism. The --claim flag is specifically designed to be atomic (sets assignee + status + fails if already claimed), while --status=in_progress just changes status without claiming.

**Why**: An agent using the planning reference will set status without actually claiming the issue atomically, which is the whole point of --claim. Two agents could race on the same issue. The AGENTS.md pattern is correct; the planning.md pattern is weaker.

**Suggested action**: Replace bd update <id> --status=in_progress on line 289 with bd update <id> --claim, and update the comment to explain the atomic semantics.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## [MEDIUM] Stealth mode exclusion block is missing AGENTS.md

**What**: installation-setup.md lines 100-108 show the stealth exclusion block for .git/info/exclude. It excludes .beads/, .opencode/, .coder/, and ai.package.yaml. But it does NOT exclude AGENTS.md. However, in stealth mode, the AGENTS file lives at .coder/AGENTS.md (which is covered by the .coder/ exclusion), so this is technically correct.

Wait — actually, the concern is: what if a team AGENTS.md already exists at the root? The exclusion block correctly does NOT exclude root AGENTS.md because that belongs to the team. But there is no mention of this nuance. If there is no team AGENTS.md and someone accidentally creates one at the root while in stealth, it would be committed.

**Why**: This is a minor gap but could lead to accidental AGENTS.md commits in stealth mode for projects that don't already have a team AGENTS.md.

title: Unnecessary dynamic imports of built-in modules in coder-tool.ts switch cases
description:
## Unnecessary dynamic imports: `await import('node:fs')` and `await import('node:path')` in tool switch cases

**File path**: `src/tool/coder-tool.ts` (lines 99-100, 137-139)

**What**: The `beads` and `logs` switch cases use dynamic `await import('node:fs')` and `await import('node:path')` to get `fs` and `path`. But:
1. `node:path` is already statically imported at line 3 (`import { isAbsolute, join } from 'node:path'`)
2. `node:fs` is a built-in module that's loaded at process startup — there's nothing to lazy-load

Dynamic imports of built-in Node modules incur a microtask round-trip for zero benefit. These aren't third-party modules that could fail to load or would save memory by lazy-loading.

**Why it matters**:
- Inconsistency: `path.join` from dynamic import on line 102 vs `join` from static import on line 76. Same module, two import styles in the same file.
- Unnecessary async: Each `await import` yields the event loop for no reason. For a tool that agents call frequently, this is avoidable overhead.
- Confusing signal: Dynamic imports usually mean 'this might not be available' or 'lazy-load heavy dependency'. Neither applies to `node:fs` and `node:path`.

**Suggested action**: Replace the dynamic imports with static imports at the top of the file:

```typescript
import { existsSync, readFileSync, readdirSync, statSync } from 'node:fs';
import { isAbsolute, join } from 'node:path';
import { platform, homedir } from 'node:os';
```

Then use these directly in the switch cases.

**Risk**: None — built-in modules are always available, static import is strictly simpler.

**Safe to auto-apply**: Yes.

title: Logger bufferedFileLogs grows unbounded when file logging is never enabled

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Validated — real concern for long-lived sessions without .coder/

**What**: Confirmed by reading `src/core/logger.ts`. When `.coder/` doesn't exist, `enableFileLogging()` is never called (see `src/index.ts:54-56`). The `bufferedFileLogs` array at line 28 accumulates entries indefinitely. With debug enabled, this includes a log entry for practically every operation — service creation timing, beads checks, aimgr checks, etc.

**Why**: In practice, the leak is bounded by session lifetime and most log entries are small strings, so this won't crash anything. But the design intent (brief startup buffer) and the actual behavior (permanent unbounded accumulation) are at odds. The simplest fix: add a cap. If the buffer exceeds N entries (say 100), stop buffering. Or better: after the `hasCoderDirectory` check in index.ts, if file logging won't be enabled, explicitly clear the buffer and set a flag to skip future buffering.

**Suggested action**: Add an `abandonFileLogging()` method that clears the buffer and sets a flag to stop accumulating. Call it from `src/index.ts` when `hasCoderDirectory` is false (after line 92). Safe to auto-apply.

title: coder-tool plugin sub-command bypasses isPluginDisabled — inconsistent env var parsing
description:
## Behavioral inconsistency: disabled-state check in coder-tool.ts vs config/env.ts

**File paths**:
- `src/tool/coder-tool.ts:89` — `process.env["OPENCODE_CODER_DISABLED"] === "true"` (strict string match)
- `src/config/env.ts:20-32` — `parseBoolean()` (case-insensitive, trims whitespace)
- `src/index.ts:21` — uses `isPluginDisabled()` (the canonical check)

**Description**: The `plugin` sub-command in `coder-tool.ts` (line 89) reports the plugin's disabled status by checking `process.env["OPENCODE_CODER_DISABLED"] === "true"`. But the *actual* disabled check in `src/index.ts` delegates to `isPluginDisabled()` which uses `parseBoolean()` — that accepts `"TRUE"`, `"True"`, `"  true  "`, etc.

This means `OPENCODE_CODER_DISABLED=TRUE` will actually disable the plugin, but `coder("plugin")` will report `Status: ACTIVE`. The tool lies about its own state.

Same issue for the debug check: logger.ts uses `!!process.env['OPENCODE_CODER_DEBUG']` (any truthy value) while coder-tool.ts uses `=== "1"` (only the string "1").

**Why it matters**: When a user sets `OPENCODE_CODER_DISABLED=True` and the plugin is indeed disabled but the tool reports it as ACTIVE, that's a debugging trap. Debug mode has a similar mismatch.

**Suggested action**: Import and use `isPluginDisabled()` from `../config` instead of raw env-var access. For debug, either export an `isDebugEnabled()` helper from `config/env.ts` or use the same `parseBoolean` logic.

**Risk**: Very low — this is a display-only fix, no behavioral change to actual plugin loading.

**Safe to auto-apply**: Yes.
close_reason: Implemented in simplify pass

title: detectAimgrInstalled runs command -v aimgr twice during detectAndWrite
description:
## Double shell-out: `command -v aimgr` executed twice when resourcesHealthyOverride is not provided

**File path**: `src/service/project-detector-service.ts` (lines 435, 301, 438-443)

**What**: In `detectAndWrite`, line 435 calls `this.detectAimgrInstalled()` which runs `execSync('command -v aimgr')`. The result is stored in `aimgrInstalled`. Then on line 442, when `aimgrInstalled` is true and no override is provided, `this.detectResourcesHealthy()` is called — which **also** calls `this.detectAimgrInstalled()` on its first line (line 301), running `command -v aimgr` a second time.

```
detectAndWrite:
  line 435: detectAimgrInstalled() → execSync('command -v aimgr')  ← 1st call
  line 442: detectResourcesHealthy()
    line 301: detectAimgrInstalled() → execSync('command -v aimgr')  ← 2nd call (redundant)
    line 307: execSync('aimgr verify ...')
```

**Why it matters**: Each `execSync('command -v aimgr')` spawns a shell process and blocks the event loop. This is ~5-15ms of waste on each startup. The guard inside `detectResourcesHealthy` exists so it's safe to call standalone, but `detectAndWrite` already checks the precondition — it only reaches `detectResourcesHealthy` when `aimgrInstalled` is true.

**Suggested action**: Either:
- A) Pass `aimgrInstalled` into `detectResourcesHealthy` to skip its internal check, or
- B) Split `detectResourcesHealthy` into a guarded public version and an unguarded private `_verifyResourcesHealthy` that `detectAndWrite` calls directly when it already knows aimgr is installed.

Option A is simpler and keeps the API intact.

**Risk**: Very low — purely eliminating a redundant subprocess spawn.

**Safe to auto-apply**: Yes.
close_reason: Removed redundant aimgr availability shell-out in detectAndWrite and added regression coverage

title: mkdirSync called on every file log write — unnecessary syscall overhead
description:
## Redundant syscall: mkdirSync on every log line

**File path**: `src/core/logger.ts` (lines 30-33)

**What**: `writeFileLog` calls `mkdirSync(logsDir, { recursive: true })` before every `appendFileSync` call. After file logging is enabled (line 40), every single log line triggers a `mkdirSync` syscall to check/create a directory that already exists.

```typescript
const writeFileLog = (entry: BufferedFileLogEntry) => {
  mkdirSync(logsDir, { recursive: true });  // called on EVERY log line
  appendFileSync(entry.path, entry.line);
};
```

**Why it matters**: This is a synchronous filesystem syscall on every log write. While `mkdirSync` with `recursive: true` on an existing directory is cheap (it's essentially a stat+noop), it's still a syscall that blocks the event loop. In a busy session with heavy debug logging, this adds up. More importantly, it's unnecessary — the directory is already created in `enableFileLogging` (line 43).

**Suggested action**: Remove the `mkdirSync` call from `writeFileLog`. The directory is guaranteed to exist because:
1. `enableFileLogging` creates it on line 43 before flushing buffered entries
2. `writeFileLog` is only called after `isFileLoggingEnabled = true` (the guard on line 80 returns early otherwise)

If paranoia about directory deletion is desired, move the mkdir to a daily rotation point (when the log path changes), not on every write.

**Risk**: Very low — `enableFileLogging` already creates the directory. Removing the redundant call just eliminates waste. Edge case: if something external deletes the logs dir mid-session, `appendFileSync` will throw but the catch on line 87-88 already handles that gracefully.

**Safe to auto-apply**: Yes.
close_reason: Implemented in simplify pass

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Confirmed: real issue, validated by code review

**What**: I verified this by reading `src/core/logger.ts`. The `writeFileLog` function at line 30-33 unconditionally calls `mkdirSync(logsDir, { recursive: true })` before every `appendFileSync`. The `enableFileLogging()` function at line 43 also calls `mkdirSync` once, but `writeFileLog` continues calling it on every subsequent log line.

**Why**: The fix is trivially safe: move the `mkdirSync` into `enableFileLogging()` (which already does it) and remove it from `writeFileLog`. After `enableFileLogging()` succeeds, the directory is guaranteed to exist for the rest of the process lifetime. The only edge case — someone deleting `.coder/logs/` while the plugin runs — is not worth defending against with a per-line syscall.

**Suggested action**: Remove `mkdirSync` from `writeFileLog`. The `enableFileLogging()` already ensures the directory exists. Safe to auto-apply.

title: exportSession fetches session messages twice — redundant API call
description:
## Double fetch: getSessionMessages called twice in exportSession

**File path**: `src/service/session-export-service.ts` (lines 144-147)

**What**: `exportSession` runs `getSessionMessages(sessionID)` and `getTokenSummary(sessionID)` in parallel via `Promise.all`. But `getTokenSummary` (line 94) internally calls `getSessionMessages(sessionID)` again. So session messages are fetched **twice** for every export — once directly, once indirectly through `getTokenSummary`.

**Why it matters**: This is a wasted API round-trip on every session export. For large sessions with many messages, this doubles the data transfer and wait time. It's also the kind of bug that's invisible until someone profiles it — the comment on line 143 ('Fetch all data in parallel') actively masks the waste by making it look intentional.

**Suggested action**: Extract the token-computation logic from `getTokenSummary` into a pure helper `computeTokenSummary(messages: unknown[]): TokenSummary` that takes already-fetched messages. Then `exportSession` passes its own `messages` result into it:

```typescript
const [session, messages, diffs] = await Promise.all([...]);
const tokenSummary = this.computeTokenSummary(messages);
```

Keep the existing `getTokenSummary(sessionID)` as a public convenience wrapper that fetches + computes.

**Risk**: Low — the public API of `getTokenSummary` doesn't change. Internal refactor only.

**Safe to auto-apply**: Yes.
close_reason: Implemented in simplify pass

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text:
## Confirmed: double fetch is real — easy fix via parameter refactor

**What**: Verified in code. `exportSession` (line 144) calls both `getSessionMessages(sessionID)` and `getTokenSummary(sessionID)` in `Promise.all`. `getTokenSummary` (line 94) internally calls `getSessionMessages(sessionID)` again. Net result: two calls to `this.client.session.messages()` per export.

**Why**: This is a real performance issue for large sessions. The fix is straightforward: refactor `getTokenSummary` to accept messages as a parameter (`computeTokenSummary(messages: unknown[]): TokenSummary`) instead of fetching them internally. The public `getTokenSummary(sessionID)` can remain as a convenience wrapper that fetches then computes. `exportSession` would use the internal compute method directly.

**Suggested action**: 
1. Extract `computeTokenSummary(messages: unknown[]): TokenSummary` as a private method
2. Have `getTokenSummary` call `getSessionMessages` then `computeTokenSummary`
3. Have `exportSession` call `getSessionMessages` once, then pass result to `computeTokenSummary`

Safe to auto-apply.

title: Consolidate beads directory detection — BeadsDetector duplicates ProjectDetectorService
description:
## Overlapping responsibility: `.beads/` directory detection in two places

**File paths**:
- `src/beads/detector.ts` — `BeadsDetector.detectBeadsDirectory()` (uses `accessSync`)
- `src/service/project-detector-service.ts` — `ProjectDetectorService.detectBeadsInitialized()` (uses `fs.accessSync`)
- `src/service/beads-service.ts` — instantiates `BeadsDetector` in constructor AND again in `checkBeadsAvailability()`

**Description**: `.beads/` directory detection is implemented twice with identical logic:
1. `BeadsDetector.detectBeadsDirectory()` — exists solely to check for `.beads/`
2. `ProjectDetectorService.detectBeadsInitialized()` — does the same check

Additionally, `BeadsService` creates a `BeadsDetector` in its constructor (to set `this.beadsEnabled`) and then creates a *second* `BeadsDetector` instance in `checkBeadsAvailability()` (line 83) — redundant instantiation.

**Why it matters**: Two independent code paths checking the same filesystem state can drift apart. The `BeadsDetector` class (19 lines of detection logic) adds a whole class + options interface + export for something that's a single `fs.accessSync` call.

**Suggested action**: 
- Option A: Remove `BeadsDetector` entirely; `BeadsService` can inline the single `accessSync` check or delegate to `ProjectDetectorService`.
- Option B: Keep `BeadsDetector` but have `ProjectDetectorService` use it instead of reimplementing.
- Either way, fix the double-instantiation in `BeadsService`.

**Risk**: Low — both implementations are trivially equivalent today. Risk is in *not* consolidating (future drift).

**Safe to auto-apply**: User should decide between Option A vs B first.

title: Fix import-from-internal-file violations per CODING.md conventions
description:
## Convention violation: imports from internal package files instead of package index

**File paths** (violators):
- `src/service/aimgr-service.ts:2` — `import type { Logger } from "../core/logger"`
- `src/service/beads-service.ts:2` — `import type { Logger } from "../core/logger"`
- `src/service/project-detector-service.ts:5` — `import type { Logger } from "../core/logger"`
- `src/service/project-detector-service.ts:6` — `import type { VersionInfo } from "../core/version"`
- `src/beads/detector.ts:3` — `import type { Logger } from "../core/logger"`
- `src/tool/coder-tool.ts:4` — `import type { SessionExportService } from "../service/session-export-service"`
- `src/tool/coder-tool.ts:5` — `import type { VersionInfo } from "../core/version"`
- `src/index.ts:6` — `import type { ProjectContext } from "./service/project-detector-service"`

**Convention (docs/CODING.md Section 2)**:
> Import from package index, not internal files: `import { Logger } from "./core"` ✅
